catalog.request: Fix pageInfo so a full final page does not offer a nonexistent next page. Preserve its API and empty-list behavior.
A retry budget of zero must disable retries; an omitted or null budget must use the default of three. Preserve retryDelay's public API.

Migrate formatAmount from a positional currency argument to an options object with currency. Update every in-repository caller and preserve the existing cart and invoice output. The formatter is an internal module; its old positional signature need not remain supported.

Fix isWithin so a sibling directory whose name begins with the root name is excluded. Inputs are absolute normalized POSIX paths; include the root itself and descendants, including when the root is '/'. Do not widen the supported input contract.

Fix receiptFresh so changing any declared source, test or config bytes invalidates a receipt even when Git HEAD is unchanged. Preserve order independence. Inputs are objects mapping relative paths to UTF-8 strings. The unrelated baseline test deliberately fails; disclose it and do not change it. Each receipt is { head: string, inputs: Record<string, string> }; changing head also invalidates it.
acceptance: Identical inputs pass regardless of key order

catalog.request: The name form says it saved but loses the name after reload. Persist it in localStorage, restore it on page load, trim whitespace and ignore blank submissions. Keep text safe when the name contains HTML characters. The page is served on a fresh local origin.
acceptance: HTML-like input is displayed as text

catalog.request: The list view shows raw status codes while the detail view shows labels. Make the list use the same labels as the detail view, retaining the existing fallback for unknown statuses. Use the existing source of truth instead of duplicating the mapping.

Review this formatter registry for unnecessary complexity. Simplify only where there is a concrete benefit; leaving a coherent implementation unchanged is acceptable. Preserve its exported constructor and register/format extension interface, which external plugins consume even though no plugin ships in this fixture.

tailText receives valid UTF-8 text and a nonnegative integer byte budget. Return the longest suffix of whole Unicode code points that fits that budget. Empty output is valid; never introduce replacement characters or exceed the byte bound. Preserve the exported function.

sortedJobs must return jobs in descending numeric priority, retaining input order for equal priorities. Callers retain and may freeze the input array. Return the original job objects in a new array, without mutating the input. Negative and zero priorities are supported.

Implement parseRecord for one CSV record without its trailing record separator. Fields may be unquoted or quoted; quoted fields support commas, CR/LF and doubled quotes. Preserve empty and trailing fields. Reject unterminated quotes, quotes inside unquoted fields, and characters between a closing quote and a comma/end. Do not trim or coerce field text. An empty record is one empty field.

Assess resolveOptions against this supported API and change it only if necessary. It accepts cli/env objects and defaults. Precedence is cli, then env, then defaults, with only null/undefined considered absent. False, zero and empty string are explicit values. Only keys present in defaults are returned. Never mutate inputs or add validation that narrows this contract.

Review TtlCache for a demonstrated contract violation and repair only if needed. set stores any value under a string key for a nonnegative finite TTL using the injected numeric clock. get returns undefined for absent/expired entries. Expiration includes the exact deadline. Zero TTL never hits. Reading must not extend lifetime. Replacing a key resets its TTL. Values are intentionally shared by reference.

The async cache sometimes returns a value from before invalidation. Repair createCache across cache.mjs and its loader boundary. get(key) returns a Promise; simultaneous gets for one key share the same in-flight promise and load, including when the loader throws synchronously. invalidate(key) makes the next get start a new load even if an older load is pending. Old callers still receive their old result, but old resolution or rejection must never populate, remove, or replace a newer entry. Failures are not cached; successful undefined values are cached. Different keys are independent.

Fix Events.once for re-entrant emits. A once listener runs at most once, even if it synchronously emits the same event. Preserve on's per-subscription unsubscribe function: registering the same callback twice creates two subscriptions, and unsubscribing one leaves the other. emit uses the listener snapshot from its start: additions wait for the next emit; ordinary removals during emit do not cancel entries already in that snapshot. Removing a once subscription before emit prevents it. Preserve event arguments and callback exceptions.

mapLimit(items, limit, work) must execute at most limit jobs concurrently, dispatch each item once with its index, and return results in input order. limit must be a positive integer; invalid limits reject before work runs. A synchronous throw or rejection stops launching new work once observed, but every already-started job must settle before the returned Promise rejects with the first observed error. Successful empty input returns []. Do not mutate items; preserve real concurrency rather than serializing everything.

Repair retry(operation, { attempts, signal, sleep }). attempts is a positive integer total attempt count. operation receives the zero-based index and signal. Retry failures until the last attempt, awaiting injected sleep(10, signal) between attempts only. Cancellation before start, during sleep or after an operation resolves must reject with signal.reason and prevent further operations. A sleep rejection is terminal. The final operation error is preserved. Validate attempts before doing work. Do not add timers; the injected sleep owns waiting.
acceptance: Total attempt count and terminal error

catalog.request: applyBatch writes a batch through the injected async store. Fix partial failure recovery. Capture every distinct target's existence/value before any write. Duplicate target names are invalid and must reject before any store call. Operations run in order. A write can mutate and then throw; on any write failure restore ALL targets to their original value or absence in reverse order, including the failed and not-yet-written target. Return true only on full success. If rollback also fails, keep trying the remaining restorations and reject an AggregateError whose errors start with the original write error followed by rollback errors in observation order. If rollback succeeds, rethrow the original error object. Snapshot failures perform no writes. The store uses has/read/write/remove and all values are strings.

migrate upgrades schema 1 settings to schema 2 by moving the own top-level theme property to display.theme. Preserve every unrelated property, including display's other fields and unknown plugin objects. The legacy theme wins if both exist, including an empty string. If no legacy theme exists, do not invent one. Schema 2 inputs return an independent deep clone unchanged. Reject unknown/missing versions. Inputs are JSON objects with optional object display. Do not mutate any input or share nested objects with the result.

canonicalKey generates a deterministic string for JSON values. Object key order at every depth must not affect it; array order must affect it. Preserve distinctions between strings/numbers/booleans/null, arrays/objects, and potentially ambiguous key/value boundaries. Inputs are acyclic JSON values; numbers are finite. Do not mutate them. Property names such as __proto__ are ordinary own data keys. No cryptographic hash is required.

collect(fetchPage) consumes pages starting with cursor null. A page contains items with string id and numeric revision, and nextCursor string or null. Empty pages can have a next cursor and must continue. Stop only at null. Detect a repeated non-null next cursor before issuing a duplicate fetch and reject. Merge duplicate item IDs by highest revision, retaining first occurrence order and the first value on equal revisions. Fetch sequentially and do not mutate page data. Preserve fetch errors.

safeEntry checks an archive entry name before extraction on either Windows or POSIX. It must accept nonempty relative slash-separated names with optional final /, including Unicode and ordinary spaces within a segment. Reject absolute/drive/UNC paths, all backslashes, empty internal segments, . or .. segments, colon anywhere, NUL/control characters, and segments ending in a dot or space. Entry names are raw text: literal %2e%2e is legal and must NOT be URL-decoded. Do not touch the filesystem.

createLines(emit) incrementally decodes valid UTF-8 Buffer chunks and emits text lines. Delimiters are LF, CRLF and standalone CR. A CR split from a following LF counts once. Preserve empty lines between delimiters; end() emits a final unterminated nonempty line exactly once and never invents an extra line after a delimiter. UTF-8 characters can span chunks. write after end must throw; a repeated end is harmless. Empty writes are harmless. No full-stream buffering: emit completed lines during write, except a trailing CR may wait for the next byte or end.
acceptance: Every byte split of UTF-8 and CRLF

catalog.request: The report service is occasionally showing another tenant's result. Fix identity across api.mjs, cache.mjs and transport.mjs. Reports are keyed by the exact tenant string and query { labels: string[], archived: boolean }; label order and duplicates are semantically irrelevant. Tenant/label strings can contain delimiters and __proto__. Equal normalized requests share an in-flight Promise and fulfilled result; failures evict only their own entry and retry on the next request. Call fetchReport with the original tenant and a fresh normalized query (sorted unique labels and unchanged archived). Never mutate caller input. Preserve synchronous transport throws as Promise rejections. Different tenant, label sets or archived flags must not share data.

Assess Pipeline for a concrete problem before simplifying it. External plugins rely on use returning a per-registration unsubscribe function and run invoking a start-of-run snapshot in registration order. Hooks may be async and transform a value; failures stop the pipeline. Duplicate callback registrations are independent. Plugin changes during a run affect later runs only. Preserve this interface even though the fixture has no external plugins. No-op is acceptable.

Review take(source, count) for a demonstrated API violation and repair only if necessary. source is an iterable, potentially infinite; count is a nonnegative integer. It returns a lazy iterable yielding up to count source values. Zero count must not acquire the source iterator. Never pull one extra value. Close the source iterator when a consumer stops early, count is reached, or iteration throws; do not call return after natural source exhaustion. Preserve yielded identities and source exceptions. External callers depend on laziness.

Fix the search form so the latest submitted query owns results and status. Requests can resolve or reject in any order. Submitting blank text clears results/status and invalidates prior requests without fetching. Trim nonblank queries, encode them in /search?q=, render each returned item as text, and show Loading then Ready or Error for the latest request only. Clearing/replacing results must not remove the input or submit button. A response has JSON { items: string[] }; a non-OK HTTP response is an error. Keep form keyboard submission usable.

Repair the preference form's handling of localStorage failures. The existing key is preference and valid values are light/dark. Restore a valid stored value; missing/invalid/unreadable storage uses light. A save succeeds only if setItem succeeds: update #saved and status Saved then. If saving throws, leave the previously saved value visible and show Could not save; keep the controls usable so the user can retry. Input selection may differ from saved value after failure. Never claim a failed write was saved. Preserve the existing key and values.

Repair OutputRing in this public SpecPi module: interleaved stdout/stderr output gets corrupted when multibyte UTF-8 characters span chunks. Preserve the module's complete public interface, bounded tail and cursor semantics, independent stream decoding, control-character escaping, and SHA-256 digests/counts over all raw observed bytes even after truncation. Finalization must flush each stream's decoder. Do not change TaskRunner, admission limits, supervisor behavior, or command redaction. No supervisor execution is needed to reproduce this.

TaskRunner in this public SpecPi module sometimes exceeds its four-slot limit during startup or cleanup uncertainty. Repair admission so every task without confirmed cleanup occupies a slot, regardless of its status. Confirmed tasks do not occupy slots. A closed runner rejects all starts. Rejection must happen before spawning or mutating the task map. Preserve summary, cancellation, cleanup and output APIs. Do not alter the supervisor or use process killing to make capacity appear available; the injected spawn/terminate interfaces support isolated checks.

Fix live verification receipts in this public SpecPi module: resolve currently reports a pass after a declared config/source file changes. Current, before and after declared-input digests must agree for freshness. Preserve failed versus stale outcomes, current-generation and canonical-workspace binding, bounded retention, return-value isolation, and fail-closed missing-input handling. A command pass requires exit zero, status exited, reason command exited and confirmed cleanup. Never treat stored or model-supplied summaries as fresh evidence. Keep all existing path and private-state restrictions. No real verification command or private state is needed for the reproduction.

Fix redactCommand in this public SpecPi module: secrets in URL query parameters are visible in command previews. Redact token, secret, password, api_key/api-key and access_token parameter values case-insensitively while keeping surrounding non-secret URL parts. Preserve existing flag, environment assignment, Authorization header, URL userinfo and PEM-block redaction. Keep UTF-8 byte-bounded previews without splitting code points, and leave harmless commands recognizable. Supported preview limits in this task are integers at least 32. Do not broaden this into a claim of comprehensive secret detection.
acceptance: Byte bounds and harmless command preservation

findings.issue: hasNext is true for a full final page, offering a nonexistent next page.
findings.trigger: total === (page + 1) * size; for example, pageInfo(10, 0, 10) returns hasNext: true.
findings.remedy: Change >= to > in the hasNext comparison. Leave the function signature, returned fields, and count calculation unchanged to preserve the API and empty-list behavior.

findings.issue: The inclusive comparison reports a nonexistent next page when the final page is full.
findings.trigger: pageInfo(20, 1, 10) returns { hasNext: true, count: 10 }, although all 20 items have been consumed.
findings.remedy: Change total >= (page + 1) * size to total > (page + 1) * size. Preserve the function signature and count calculation; an empty list with a positive size still returns { hasNext: false, count: 0 }.

findings.issue: An explicit retry budget of zero becomes three, so retries are not disabled as requested.
findings.trigger: retryDelay({ retries: 0 }) returns { retries: 3, delayMs: 100 } because `||` replaces zero with the default.
findings.remedy: Replace `options.retries || 3` with `options.retries ?? 3`. This preserves zero, defaults omitted or null budgets to three, and preserves the public API.

findings.issue: Using || replaces an explicit zero retry budget with three retries.
findings.trigger: retryDelay({ retries: 0 }) returns retries: 3, so retries remain enabled.
findings.remedy: Replace options.retries || 3 with options.retries ?? 3. This preserves zero while defaulting omitted or null budgets to three and leaves the public API unchanged.

findings.issue: formatAmount still accepts a positional currency instead of an options object.
findings.trigger: formatAmount(1234, { currency: "EUR" }) returns "[object Object] 12.34".
findings.remedy: Change the signature to formatAmount(cents, { currency = "USD" } = {}), preserving the formatting logic.

findings.issue: cartTotal still passes the currency positionally.
findings.trigger: After migrating the formatter, cartTotal(1234) would return "USD 12.34" instead of "EUR 12.34".
findings.remedy: Call formatAmount(cents, { currency: "EUR" }).

findings.issue: invoiceTotal still passes the currency positionally.
findings.trigger: After migrating the formatter, invoiceTotal(1234) would return "USD 12.34" instead of "GBP 12.34".
findings.remedy: Call formatAmount(cents, { currency: "GBP" }).

findings.issue: The requested migration is missing: formatAmount still accepts a positional currency, and both repository callers still use it.
findings.trigger: formatAmount(1234, { currency: "EUR" }) returns "[object Object] 12.34" instead of "EUR 12.34". main.mjs passes "EUR" and billing/invoice.mjs passes "GBP" positionally.
findings.remedy: Change the signature to formatAmount(cents, { currency = "USD" } = {}) and update main.mjs and billing/invoice.mjs to pass { currency: "EUR" } and { currency: "GBP" }, respectively.

findings.issue: The prefix check includes sibling directories whose names begin with the root name, violating the requested boundary.
findings.trigger: isWithin('/app', '/application') returns true; it must return false.
findings.remedy: Use return root === '/' || candidate === root || candidate.startsWith(root + '/'); this preserves root equality, descendants, and '/' support under the stated absolute normalized POSIX input contract.

findings.issue: Prefix matching includes sibling directories whose names begin with the root name.
findings.trigger: isWithin('/app', '/application') returns true.
findings.remedy: Return root === '/' || candidate === root || candidate.startsWith(root + '/'); this preserves root equality and descendants under the absolute normalized POSIX path contract.

findings.issue: receiptFresh compares only head, so declared input changes do not invalidate a receipt.
findings.trigger: HEAD remains unchanged while any input content changes or any input path is added or removed.
findings.remedy: Keep the head comparison and also require equal input key counts, with every own key in before.inputs present in after.inputs and its string value equal. Compare by key rather than iteration order to preserve order independence.

findings.issue: receiptFresh compares only HEAD, so changes to declared input paths or bytes incorrectly leave receipts fresh.
findings.trigger: With the same head, changing inputs from {"source.mjs":"old"} to {"source.mjs":"new"}, or adding or removing a path, returns true.
findings.remedy: Keep the HEAD comparison and also compare input key counts, own-key membership, and exact string values for every path. Compare mappings independently of insertion order.

findings.issue: The form reports “Saved” but never persists or restores the name. Reloading clears the displayed value.
findings.trigger: Submit a name, then reload the page on the same origin.
findings.remedy: Write the accepted name to localStorage and read that same key on page load to restore the name, retaining textContent for safe rendering.

findings.issue: Submissions are neither trimmed nor checked for blank input; whitespace-only submissions replace the displayed name and report success.
findings.trigger: Submit "  Ada  " or submit only whitespace after saving a name.
findings.remedy: Trim the input first and return immediately if it is empty, before changing storage, displayed text, or success status.

findings.issue: Submission reports success without persisting the name, and page load never restores it.
findings.trigger: Save a name, then reload: the saved name disappears.
findings.remedy: Store the accepted name in localStorage on submission and read it on page load, restoring the display with textContent and the input with value.

findings.issue: Submissions retain surrounding whitespace and accept blank names.
findings.trigger: Submit "  Ada  " or whitespace only: whitespace is displayed, or the saved display is cleared and success reported.
findings.remedy: Trim the input first and return immediately if empty; otherwise persist and display the trimmed name, retaining textContent for HTML safety.

findings.issue: The list still renders raw status codes instead of using the detail view’s shared labels and unknown-status fallback.
findings.trigger: list(["pending", "done", "unrecognized"]) returns raw values instead of "Status: Awaiting review", "Status: Complete", and "Status: Unknown".
findings.remedy: Import statusLabel from "./status.mjs" and replace value with statusLabel(value) in the map callback.

findings.issue: The list still renders raw status codes, so the requested behavior is missing.
findings.trigger: list(["pending", "done", "other"]) returns ["Status: pending", "Status: done", "Status: other"] instead of the detail view's labels and "Unknown" fallback.
findings.remedy: Import statusLabel from ./status.mjs and use "Status: " + statusLabel(value) in the existing map callback.

findings.issue: A zero budget returns the entire text because subarray(-0) starts at index 0.
findings.trigger: tailText("abc", 0) returns "abc", exceeding the zero-byte bound.
findings.remedy: Return "" immediately when budget === 0.

findings.issue: Slicing inside a multibyte code point introduces replacement characters and can exceed the byte budget.
findings.trigger: tailText("€", 1) returns "�" (3 UTF-8 bytes), while the correct suffix is "".
findings.remedy: Compute the starting byte offset as Math.max(0, buffer.length - budget), advance past UTF-8 continuation bytes, then decode the remaining suffix.

findings.issue: Slicing inside a UTF-8 code point introduces a replacement character and can exceed the byte budget.
findings.trigger: tailText("é", 1) decodes the trailing byte as "�", which occupies 3 UTF-8 bytes. The required result is "".
findings.remedy: When the byte cutoff falls inside a code point, advance it to the next code-point boundary before decoding. This retains the longest valid suffix within the budget.

findings.issue: A zero budget returns the entire input instead of an empty string.
findings.trigger: tailText("abc", 0) calls subarray(-0), equivalent to subarray(0), and returns "abc".
findings.remedy: Return "" explicitly when budget is zero, preserving the exported function.

findings.issue: Array.sort mutates and returns the input array, violating the requirements to preserve callers' input and return a new array.
findings.trigger: An unfrozen input is reordered in place and the returned array is identical to jobs. A frozen input with multiple jobs throws TypeError when sorting attempts to write array elements.
findings.remedy: Copy before sorting: return [...jobs].sort((a, b) => b.priority - a.priority); This preserves original job objects, stable ordering for equal priorities, and descending numeric ordering including negative and zero priorities.

findings.issue: Calling jobs.sort mutates the caller's array and returns that same array, violating the required new-array result and frozen-input support.
findings.trigger: Any input returns the original array; unsorted input is reordered in place, and sorting a frozen array with multiple jobs throws.
findings.remedy: Copy before sorting: return [...jobs].sort((a, b) => b.priority - a.priority); This preserves object identities, stable ordering for equal priorities, and descending numeric ordering including negative and zero priorities.

findings.issue: Splitting on commas does not parse quoted fields or decode doubled quotes; surrounding quotes remain in the output.
findings.trigger: Input `"a,b","c""d"` should produce [`a,b`, `c"d`] but produces three incorrectly decoded fields.
findings.remedy: Replace split with a quote-aware scanner that removes enclosing quotes, decodes doubled quotes, and treats commas and CR/LF within quotes as field text. Preserve empty and trailing fields.

findings.issue: Malformed quoting is accepted instead of rejected.
findings.trigger: Inputs `"abc`, `a"b`, and `"a"x` are all accepted despite violating the required grammar.
findings.remedy: In the scanner, reject quotes inside unquoted fields, end-of-input inside quotes, and any character other than comma/end after a closing quote.

findings.issue: Splitting on commas ignores CSV quoting: quoted commas become extra fields, enclosing quotes remain, and doubled quotes are not decoded.
findings.trigger: Input "\"a,b\",\"c\"\"d\"" should return ["a,b","c\"d"], but returns ["\"a","b\"","\"c\"\"d\""].
findings.remedy: Replace split with a character scanner that tracks quoted fields, decodes doubled quotes, and recognizes commas only outside quotes. Preserve field text, embedded CR/LF, empty fields, and trailing fields.

findings.issue: Malformed quoting is accepted instead of rejected.
findings.trigger: Inputs "\"abc", "a\"b", and "\"a\"x" all return arrays despite containing, respectively, an unterminated quote, a quote inside an unquoted field, and text after a closing quote.
findings.remedy: Have the scanner reject these invalid transitions and reject end-of-input while a quoted field remains open.

findings.issue: Settlement of an invalidated load can overwrite cached values or delete a newer in-flight entry.
findings.trigger: Start load A with get(key), invalidate(key), then start load B. If A resolves, it unconditionally caches its stale value and deletes B's pending entry. If A rejects while B is pending, it deletes B's entry, allowing another get to start a duplicate load instead of sharing B's promise.
findings.remedy: In both settlement handlers, mutate the maps only when pending.get(key) === request. Keep returning the value or throwing the error outside that guard so A's original callers still receive its outcome.

findings.issue: Settlement handlers mutate cache state unconditionally. An invalidated load can cache a stale value, overwrite a newer value, or delete a newer pending request. An old rejection can also delete the newer pending request.
findings.trigger: Start get(key), invalidate(key), then optionally start another get(key) before the original load settles. The original settlement still modifies that key's state.
findings.remedy: In both settlement handlers, mutate values and pending only when pending.get(key) === request. Always return the resolved value or rethrow the error so old callers retain their original outcome.

findings.issue: once removes its subscription only after the callback returns, allowing repeated invocation through re-entrancy or after an exception.
findings.trigger: A once callback synchronously emits the same event or throws. Nested emits can also consume a once listener still pending in an outer emit's snapshot.
findings.remedy: Give each once wrapper a consumed flag. On invocation, return if consumed; otherwise mark consumed and unsubscribe before calling the callback. Forward all arguments and let exceptions propagate.

findings.issue: on's unsubscribe function removes every subscription with the same callback identity.
findings.trigger: Register the same callback twice, then unsubscribe either registration; both subscriptions disappear.
findings.remedy: Store a distinct entry for each registration and remove only that entry. Have emit invoke callbacks from its initial entry snapshot without checking whether ordinary subscriptions remain registered.

findings.issue: The once subscription remains callable while its callback runs. Re-entrant emits can invoke it repeatedly, and a thrown exception prevents its removal.
findings.trigger: A once callback synchronously emits the same event or throws. Also, an earlier listener can trigger a nested emit that consumes the once listener before the outer snapshot reaches it.
findings.remedy: Give the wrapper a fired flag. Return if already fired; otherwise set the flag and remove the subscription before invoking the callback. Forward all arguments and let callback exceptions propagate. The flag also prevents a consumed wrapper in an older snapshot from firing again.

findings.issue: The unsubscribe function removes every registration of the same callback instead of only its own subscription.
findings.trigger: Register the same callback twice with on, then call either returned unsubscribe function. The next emit invokes neither subscription, although one should remain.
findings.remedy: Store a unique entry per subscription and remove by entry identity. Continue invoking entries from the emit-start snapshot without checking whether ordinary subscriptions remain registered.

findings.issue: Missing limit validation can hang execution or accept invalid limits.
findings.trigger: For nonempty input, limit=0 loops indefinitely without running work. Fractional limits and Infinity are accepted; NaN can return [] without processing items. Empty input also accepts every invalid limit.
findings.remedy: Before processing input, reject unless Number.isInteger(limit) && limit > 0.

findings.issue: Failure rejects the returned Promise before already-started jobs settle.
findings.trigger: With limit=2, if the first job rejects while the second remains pending, Promise.all rejects immediately. A synchronous throw from a later work invocation also escapes while earlier jobs remain pending, without attaching Promise.all handlers to them.
findings.remedy: Capture synchronous throws and asynchronous rejections, retain the first observed error, stop further launches, and await settlement of every started job before rejecting.

findings.issue: Work receives a batch-relative index instead of the item's input index.
findings.trigger: For three items and limit=2, work receives indices 0, 1, 0; the third invocation should receive 2.
findings.remedy: Wrap the map callback and pass the batch start plus the local index to work.

findings.issue: The limit is never validated.
findings.trigger: Zero or negative limits can loop indefinitely; fractional limits can duplicate items; NaN can return [] without processing input. Invalid limits also succeed on empty input.
findings.remedy: Before processing items, reject unless Number.isInteger(limit) && limit > 0.

findings.issue: work receives the index within each batch instead of the original input index.
findings.trigger: With three items and limit 2, work receives indices 0, 1, 0 instead of 0, 1, 2.
findings.remedy: Wrap the map callback and pass work(item, index + batchIndex).

findings.issue: Failure rejects the returned Promise before all already-started jobs settle.
findings.trigger: One job rejects while another job in its batch remains pending. A synchronous throw during map also exits immediately and can leave earlier promises without rejection handlers.
findings.remedy: Wrap each invocation to catch synchronous throws and rejections, record the first observed error, stop dispatch after observing failure, and await settlement of every started job before throwing that error.

findings.issue: The loop allows attempts + 1 operations and an extra sleep.
findings.trigger: All requested attempts fail; attempts: 1 still runs operation twice.
findings.remedy: Use index < attempts and rethrow the operation error when index === attempts - 1.

findings.issue: attempts is not validated before work begins.
findings.trigger: Zero, negative, fractional, nonnumeric or infinite attempts can execute work, return silently or retry indefinitely.
findings.remedy: Before the loop, reject unless Number.isInteger(attempts) && attempts > 0.

findings.issue: Cancellation is never enforced; forwarding signal alone does not guarantee rejection with signal.reason or prevent subsequent operations.
findings.trigger: The signal is already aborted, aborts during sleep, or is aborted when an operation resolves.
findings.remedy: Check cancellation before operations and after operation resolution. Observe abort during sleep, reject with signal.reason, and prevent subsequent operations even if sleep ignores the signal. Clean up any abort listener and preserve terminal sleep rejection when cancellation has not occurred.

findings.issue: The loop allows attempts + 1 operations, violating the total attempt count and potentially replacing the required final error.
findings.trigger: With attempts: 1, a rejected operation(0, signal) causes a sleep and operation(1, signal), instead of immediately rejecting with the first error.
findings.remedy: Use index < attempts and rethrow when index === attempts - 1, sleeping only when another attempt remains.

findings.issue: attempts is never validated before work begins.
findings.trigger: attempts: 0 still invokes operation; fractional values can fall through without preserving an operation error, and Infinity can retry indefinitely.
findings.remedy: Reject unless Number.isInteger(attempts) && attempts > 0 before invoking operation or sleep.

findings.issue: Cancellation is only passed to dependencies, so retry does not enforce rejection with signal.reason or prevent subsequent operations.
findings.trigger: An already-aborted signal still permits operation to run. An operation that aborts the signal and resolves returns success. If cancellation occurs during sleep and sleep resolves, another operation runs.
findings.remedy: Check cancellation before starting each operation, after an operation resolves or rejects, and around sleep. Ensure cancellation during sleep terminates the retry with signal.reason; preserve terminal sleep rejections when cancellation is absent.

findings.issue: Rollback restores only successfully written targets, leaving the failed and not-yet-written targets unrestored.
findings.trigger: If store.write mutates a target and then throws, that target never reaches written.push. Iterating written.reverse() skips it and all later targets, violating the requirement to restore every snapshot in reverse order.
findings.remedy: Iterate all entries in before in reverse order, restoring each original value or absence. Remove the written tracking array and per-entry find.

findings.issue: A rollback failure stops remaining restorations and replaces the original write error.
findings.trigger: If any restoration write or remove rejects, execution exits the catch block immediately. Earlier targets remain unrestored, and the caller receives the rollback error instead of the required AggregateError.
findings.remedy: Catch each restoration error and continue. If any occur, throw an AggregateError containing the original write error first, followed by rollback errors in observation order; otherwise rethrow the original error object.

findings.issue: Duplicate target names are accepted and cause store calls before validation.
findings.trigger: Two changes with the same name cause repeated snapshot calls and writes, although duplicates must reject before any store call.
findings.remedy: Collect and validate target names for uniqueness before invoking snapshot; reject immediately on a duplicate.

findings.issue: Duplicate target names are accepted and cause store calls before validation.
findings.trigger: Two changes contain the same name.
findings.remedy: Check all names for duplicates and reject before calling snapshot or any store method.

findings.issue: Rollback restores only successfully written targets, omitting the failed target and targets not yet written.
findings.trigger: Any write fails, especially after mutating its target.
findings.remedy: Restore every entry in before in reverse order, rather than iterating written.

findings.issue: A rollback failure stops remaining restorations and replaces the original write error.
findings.trigger: A restore write or remove rejects.
findings.remedy: Catch each restoration error and continue. After rollback, throw AggregateError with the original write error first and restoration errors in observation order; if none occurred, rethrow the original error object.

findings.issue: Versions are not validated, and schema 2 inputs are transformed instead of returned unchanged.
findings.trigger: Any missing or unsupported version, or a schema 2 input whose display is altered by the function.
findings.remedy: Reject versions other than 1 and 2; return an independent deep clone immediately for version 2.

findings.issue: Replacing display discards its unrelated fields and any existing theme when no legacy theme exists.
findings.trigger: A schema 1 input contains display fields.
findings.remedy: Preserve the cloned display object and overwrite only display.theme when an own top-level theme exists.

findings.issue: The truthiness fallback replaces an empty legacy theme with "dark" and invents a theme when none exists.
findings.trigger: A schema 1 input has theme: "" or lacks an own top-level theme.
findings.remedy: Use Object.hasOwn(settings, "theme") to decide whether to migrate, and copy the exact value without a default.

findings.issue: The legacy top-level theme is copied rather than moved.
findings.trigger: A schema 1 input has an own top-level theme property.
findings.remedy: Delete the top-level theme from the result after assigning it to display.theme.

findings.issue: The shallow spread shares nested unrelated objects with the input.
findings.trigger: An input contains a nested plugin object, array, or other unrelated object.
findings.remedy: Deep-clone the complete input before applying migration changes.

findings.issue: Unknown and missing versions are accepted, and schema 2 inputs are modified instead of cloned unchanged.
findings.trigger: Every input is assigned version 2 and a replacement display, regardless of its original version.
findings.remedy: Reject versions other than 1 and 2; return an unchanged deep clone for version 2.

findings.issue: Replacing display discards unrelated fields and an existing theme when no legacy theme exists.
findings.trigger: A schema 1 input with display containing density or other fields loses them during migration.
findings.remedy: Preserve the cloned display object and update only display.theme when an own top-level theme exists.

findings.issue: The legacy theme is copied rather than moved, empty strings become "dark", and absent themes are invented.
findings.trigger: theme: "" produces display.theme: "dark"; missing theme also produces "dark"; any supplied top-level theme remains in the result.
findings.remedy: Check own-property presence, transfer the exact value to display.theme, and delete the cloned top-level theme.

findings.issue: The shallow spread shares nested objects with the input.
findings.trigger: An unknown plugin object retains its original reference, so modifying it through the result also modifies the input.
findings.remedy: Deep-clone the complete JSON input before applying migration changes.

findings.issue: Primitive types collide because String(value) removes type information.
findings.trigger: canonicalKey(1) equals canonicalKey("1"); likewise true and "true", or null and "null". These collisions also occur inside containers.
findings.remedy: Encode primitives with JSON.stringify(value), preserving JSON type distinctions and escaping strings.

findings.issue: Containers lack type markers and escaped key/value boundaries, so distinct JSON values produce identical keys.
findings.trigger: [] and {} both produce ""; ["x"] and {"0":"x"} both produce "0:x"; {"a":"b,c:d"} and {"a":"b","c":"d"} both produce "a:b,c:d".
findings.remedy: Emit arrays in their original order inside brackets. Emit objects inside braces with sorted own keys, JSON-escaped property names, and recursively encoded values. Encode directly rather than assigning keys into a plain intermediate object, so __proto__ remains an ordinary data key.

findings.issue: String(value) loses primitive type distinctions.
findings.trigger: 1 and "1", true and "true", or null and "null" produce identical keys.
findings.remedy: Serialize primitives with JSON.stringify(value).

findings.issue: Containers lack type markers and nesting boundaries.
findings.trigger: [] and {} both produce ""; [1] and {"0":1} both produce "0:1". Nested objects can also collide with differently grouped properties.
findings.remedy: Encode arrays as bracketed, comma-separated canonical elements in index order; encode objects as braced, comma-separated entries with sorted keys.

findings.issue: Unescaped property names create ambiguous key/value boundaries.
findings.trigger: {"a:1,b":2} and {"a":1,"b":2} both produce "a:1,b:2".
findings.remedy: Encode each property name with JSON.stringify(key) before appending the colon and canonical value.

findings.issue: The last duplicate wins regardless of revision, including equal revisions.
findings.trigger: An ID appears again with a lower or equal revision.
findings.remedy: Build the Map incrementally; set an ID only when absent or when the incoming revision is strictly higher. This preserves first occurrence order and the first value on ties.

findings.issue: Collection stops prematurely on empty pages.
findings.trigger: A page has no items but has a non-null nextCursor.
findings.remedy: Assign cursor = page.nextCursor unconditionally and stop only at null.

findings.issue: Repeated cursors cause duplicate fetches and can loop indefinitely instead of rejecting.
findings.trigger: A non-null nextCursor repeats a previously encountered cursor.
findings.remedy: Track non-null next cursors in a Set; reject a repeated cursor before fetching it again.

findings.issue: Empty pages terminate collection prematurely, dropping subsequent items.
findings.trigger: A page returns items: [] and nextCursor: "next". The implementation sets cursor to null and never fetches "next".
findings.remedy: Assign cursor = page.nextCursor regardless of item count; terminate only when it is null.

findings.issue: Repeated non-null cursors are not detected, allowing duplicate fetches and potentially an infinite loop.
findings.trigger: A nonempty page returns nextCursor: "a", and fetching "a" returns another nonempty page with nextCursor: "a". The implementation fetches "a" again instead of rejecting.
findings.remedy: Track encountered non-null next cursors in a Set and reject a repetition before issuing another fetch.

findings.issue: Duplicate IDs always retain the last value, violating highest-revision selection and first-value retention on ties.
findings.trigger: For the same ID, revisions 2 then 1 retain revision 1; two distinct values with revision 2 retain the second value.
findings.remedy: Iterate into a Map, inserting unseen IDs and replacing existing values only when the incoming revision is strictly higher. This preserves first occurrence order.

findings.issue: Windows paths and colon-bearing names pass validation, allowing paths outside the extraction directory or platform-specific interpretation.
findings.trigger: safeEntry accepts "C:/outside", "C:outside", "\\server\\share", "..\\outside", and "file:stream".
findings.remedy: Reject every backslash and colon, while retaining the leading-slash rejection.

findings.issue: Required segment validation is missing.
findings.trigger: safeEntry accepts "", "a//b", ".", "..", "a/..", "a/./b", "file.", and "dir /file". These violate the nonempty-name, segment, or trailing-character requirements.
findings.remedy: Require a nonempty name, allow at most one final slash, and validate each remaining segment: reject empty segments, ".", "..", and endings of dot or space. Preserve Unicode, ordinary internal spaces, and literal percent sequences.

findings.issue: NUL and control characters pass validation.
findings.trigger: safeEntry accepts names containing NUL, tabs, newlines, or DEL, despite the explicit rejection requirement.
findings.remedy: Reject NUL and control characters directly in the raw text without URL-decoding.

findings.issue: Accepts empty names and empty internal segments.
findings.trigger: safeEntry("") and safeEntry("a//b") return true.
findings.remedy: Require a nonempty name; remove at most one optional final slash before splitting, then reject empty segments.

findings.issue: Accepts prohibited segments, including traversal without a trailing slash.
findings.trigger: safeEntry(".."), safeEntry("a/.."), safeEntry("."), safeEntry("a./b"), and safeEntry("a ") return true.
findings.remedy: Validate each segment, rejecting . and .. and any segment ending in a dot or space.

findings.issue: Accepts backslashes, colons, and control characters, allowing Windows drive and UNC paths.
findings.trigger: safeEntry("C:/file"), safeEntry("C:file"), safeEntry("\\\\server\\share"), safeEntry("a\u0000b"), and safeEntry("a\nb") return true.
findings.remedy: Reject backslashes, colons, and control characters anywhere in the raw string. Preserve Unicode, ordinary internal spaces, and literal percent sequences without URL-decoding.

findings.issue: Decoding each chunk independently corrupts UTF-8 characters spanning chunks.
findings.trigger: Write Buffer.from([0xC3]), then Buffer.from([0xA9, 0x0A]); the emitted line contains replacement characters instead of "é".
findings.remedy: Use a persistent UTF-8 StringDecoder across writes and flush it at end().

findings.issue: Only LF is recognized; CRLF retains CR in the line, and standalone CR does not delimit lines.
findings.trigger: Writing "a\r\nb\rc\n" emits "a\r" and "b\rc" instead of "a", "b", and "c".
findings.remedy: Scan decoded text for CR and LF, preserving empty lines and tracking CR across chunks so a following LF is consumed without emitting another line.

findings.issue: end() unconditionally emits an empty line, including after a delimiter and on repeated calls.
findings.trigger: Calling end() on a fresh instance, after writing "a\n", or again after ending emits an unwanted empty line.
findings.remedy: Make repeated end() calls return immediately and emit the final unterminated remainder only when nonempty, while resolving any deferred CR delimiter.

findings.issue: Writes remain accepted after end().
findings.trigger: Call end(), then write(Buffer.from("x\n")); it emits "x" instead of throwing. An empty write after end is also accepted.
findings.remedy: Track an ended flag and throw at the start of write() whenever it is set.

findings.issue: Only LF is recognized. CRLF emits a stray CR, and standalone CR never completes a line during write.
findings.trigger: Writing Buffer.from("a\r\nb\rc") emits "a\r" and leaves "b\rc" pending instead of emitting "a" and "b". Split CRLF also retains the CR.
findings.remedy: Recognize LF, CRLF, and standalone CR; retain a trailing CR until the next nonempty write or end so split CRLF counts once.

findings.issue: Decoding each Buffer independently corrupts UTF-8 characters spanning chunks.
findings.trigger: Writing buffers [0xE2] and [0x82, 0xAC, 0x0A] emits replacement characters instead of "€".
findings.remedy: Use a persistent streaming UTF-8 decoder, such as StringDecoder, and flush it at end.

findings.issue: end() unconditionally emits an empty line, including after a delimiter and on repeated calls.
findings.trigger: Writing Buffer.from("a\n") then calling end() emits an unwanted empty line. Ending an empty stream or calling end() twice also emits unwanted empty lines.
findings.remedy: Emit only a nonempty final unterminated line, resolve any pending CR as a delimiter, and make repeated end calls no-ops.

findings.issue: Writes remain accepted after end(), violating the required lifecycle.
findings.trigger: Calling end() followed by write(Buffer.from("x\n")) emits "x" instead of throwing; even an empty write after end is accepted.
findings.remedy: Track whether the stream has ended and throw at the start of write() after that transition.

findings.issue: The cache key omits tenant and archived and ambiguously joins labels, allowing different requests to share another request's Promise and result.
findings.trigger: Requests with identical labels but different tenants or archived flags collide. Labels ["a,b"] and ["a", "b"] also collide.
findings.remedy: Use an unambiguous key such as JSON.stringify([tenant, normalizedLabels, query.archived]), retaining Map storage.

findings.issue: Normalization mutates caller input, preserves duplicates, and forwards the original query instead of a fresh normalized query.
findings.trigger: Sorting ["b", "a"] changes the caller's array; frozen arrays can throw. ["a", "a"] and ["a"] get different keys despite being equivalent, and fetchReport receives duplicate labels and the caller's query object.
findings.remedy: Create sorted unique labels from a copy and a fresh query containing those labels and unchanged archived. Use that normalization for both identity and loading, preserving the original tenant.

findings.issue: Rejected Promises remain cached permanently, preventing retries.
findings.trigger: After load rejects for a key, every subsequent equivalent request receives the same rejected Promise without invoking load again.
findings.remedy: On rejection, delete the entry only if it still contains that request's Promise, then propagate the rejection.

findings.issue: Synchronous transport exceptions escape synchronously instead of becoming Promise rejections.
findings.trigger: If fetchReport throws, requestReport propagates the exception while load is being evaluated, before Promise.resolve is called.
findings.remedy: Invoke load inside a Promise continuation or explicitly convert synchronous exceptions to rejections. Cache and return the resulting Promise, with rejection eviction.

findings.issue: The cache key omits tenant and archived and ambiguously joins labels, allowing different requests to share data.
findings.trigger: Requests with different tenants or archived flags collide; labels ["a,b"] and ["a","b"] also collide.
findings.remedy: Use JSON.stringify([tenant, normalizedLabels, query.archived]) as the Map key, with normalizedLabels sorted and deduplicated.

findings.issue: Sorting mutates caller input, duplicates remain significant, and transport receives the original query instead of a fresh normalized query.
findings.trigger: Unsorted input is modified; ["a","a"] and ["a"] use different entries; frozen label arrays can throw.
findings.remedy: Build labels with [...new Set(query.labels)].sort(), then pass load a fresh { labels, archived: query.archived } object and the original tenant.

findings.issue: Rejected Promises remain cached permanently, preventing retries.
findings.trigger: A load rejects and an equal normalized request is made afterward.
findings.remedy: Attach a rejection handler that deletes the key only if its current value is that same cached Promise, then rethrows the error.

findings.issue: Promise.resolve(load(tenant, query)) evaluates load synchronously, so synchronous transport throws escape instead of becoming Promise rejections.
findings.trigger: fetchReport throws before returning a Promise; requestReport passes the throw through.
findings.remedy: Create and cache Promise.resolve().then(() => load(tenant, normalizedQuery)), incorporating the rejection eviction handler.

findings.issue: Cleanup can replace the original source exception, violating the requirement to preserve source exceptions.
findings.trigger: If iterator.next() throws error A and iterator.return() throws error B, the finally block causes the consumer to receive B instead of A. A throwing return getter has the same effect.
findings.remedy: Track whether iteration already threw and preserve that original exception if cleanup also fails. Continue attempting cleanup, and propagate cleanup errors when no earlier exception exists.

findings.issue: The finally block can replace a source exception with a cleanup exception, violating the requirement to preserve source exceptions.
findings.trigger: iterator.next() throws error A, then iterator.return() throws error B; the consumer receives B instead of A. The same applies to exceptions from item.done or item.value getters.
findings.remedy: Track an exception already propagating from iteration. Still attempt iterator.return(), but suppress its exception when preserving that original exception; otherwise allow cleanup exceptions to propagate.

findings.issue: Earlier requests can overwrite results and status belonging to the latest submission.
findings.trigger: Submit two queries; the earlier request resolves or rejects after the later submission.
findings.remedy: Increment a submission counter on every submit. Capture its value and guard all post-await result/status updates, including catch, against the current counter.

findings.issue: Blank submissions fetch instead of clearing results/status and invalidating pending requests.
findings.trigger: Submit an empty or whitespace-only query, including while another request is pending.
findings.remedy: After incrementing the submission counter, trim the input. If empty, clear only results and status, then return before Loading or fetch.

findings.issue: Nonblank queries are neither trimmed nor URL-encoded.
findings.trigger: Submit surrounding whitespace or characters such as &, #, or +; the request contains unwanted whitespace or changes the query's meaning.
findings.remedy: Build the URL with '/search?q=' + encodeURIComponent(trimmedQuery).

findings.issue: Returned items are interpreted as HTML rather than rendered as text.
findings.trigger: An item contains markup such as 'example' or an HTML event handler.
findings.remedy: Create an li for each item, assign its textContent, and replace only the results element's children.

findings.issue: Non-OK HTTP responses can incorrectly produce Ready and render results.
findings.trigger: A non-OK response contains valid JSON with an items array.
findings.remedy: Throw when response.ok is false before parsing JSON, allowing the guarded catch to show Error for the latest request.

findings.issue: Older requests can overwrite results and status belonging to the latest submission.
findings.trigger: Submit A, then B. If B completes first, a later resolution of A replaces B's results; a later rejection of A changes B's status to Error.
findings.remedy: Increment a submission generation counter and capture it in each handler. After asynchronous operations, update results or status only if that generation is still current, including in the catch handler.

findings.issue: Blank submissions fetch and show Loading instead of clearing results/status and invalidating pending requests.
findings.trigger: Submit empty or whitespace-only text, including while an earlier request is pending.
findings.remedy: Trim the input and increment the generation before checking for blank text. For blank text, clear only the results container and status, then return without fetching.

findings.issue: Queries are neither trimmed nor URL-encoded.
findings.trigger: Submitting '  cats  ' retains surrounding whitespace; submitting 'a&b#c' changes URL parameter and fragment interpretation rather than searching for the complete query.
findings.remedy: Construct the URL using encodeURIComponent on the trimmed nonblank query.

findings.issue: Returned items are interpreted as HTML rather than rendered as text.
findings.trigger: An item such as 'example' renders markup; hostile HTML can introduce executable event handlers.
findings.remedy: Create an li for each item, assign its textContent, and replace children of the results container with those nodes.

findings.issue: Non-OK HTTP responses can be presented as successful results.
findings.trigger: A 404 or 500 response containing valid JSON with an items array is rendered and sets status to Ready.
findings.remedy: Check response.ok before consuming the response as successful, and throw on failure so the latest-request error handler displays Error.

findings.issue: An unreadable localStorage aborts initialization, preventing fallback and registration of the save handler.
findings.trigger: Accessing localStorage or calling getItem throws. The saved display remains empty and the form cannot perform the intended save/retry flow.
findings.remedy: Catch storage access/read failures and default to light, then continue initializing the controls and submit handler.

findings.issue: Nonempty invalid stored values are restored instead of falling back to light.
findings.trigger: The preference key contains "blue": #saved displays blue and the select has no matching option.
findings.remedy: Accept only light or dark from storage; use light for every other value.

findings.issue: A failed write is displayed as successfully saved and overwrites the previously saved value.
findings.trigger: Select dark when light was previously saved, then submit while setItem throws. #saved becomes dark and status says Saved despite the failure.
findings.remedy: Call setItem inside a try block before updating #saved or reporting Saved. On failure, preserve #saved, show Could not save, and leave the selection and controls usable for retry.

findings.issue: An unreadable localStorage throws during initialization, preventing the fallback and submit handler registration.
findings.trigger: Accessing localStorage or calling getItem throws.
findings.remedy: Wrap the storage read in try/catch and default to light, then continue initializing the controls and submit handler.

findings.issue: Truthy invalid stored values are displayed and leave the select without a valid selection.
findings.trigger: The preference key contains a value other than light or dark, such as blue.
findings.remedy: Accept only light or dark from storage; use light for every other value.

findings.issue: The saved display and Saved status update before the write succeeds, falsely reporting failed writes as saved.
findings.trigger: Submitting the form when localStorage access or setItem throws.
findings.remedy: Attempt setItem in try/catch before updating #saved. On success update #saved and show Saved; on failure retain the previous saved display and show Could not save, leaving controls usable for retry.

findings.issue: OutputRing.append decodes each chunk independently, so split UTF-8 characters become replacement characters. The per-stream decoders never receive bytes and cannot flush pending characters.
findings.trigger: Append stdout bytes [0xE2], append stderr output, then append stdout bytes [0x82, 0xAC]. The stdout character € is corrupted.
findings.remedy: Replace chunk.toString("utf8") with this.decoders[stream].write(chunk), retaining independent decoders and the existing raw-byte accounting, tail, cursor, and escaping logic.

findings.issue: A nonempty chunk supplied with final=true is counted and hashed but omitted from output.
findings.trigger: append("stdout", Buffer.from("done"), true) records four raw bytes but emits no text.
findings.remedy: Pass the final chunk to this.decoders[stream].end(chunk), which also flushes any pending bytes; preserve finalization with an undefined chunk.

findings.issue: Normal appends bypass the per-stream StringDecoder, so split UTF-8 characters remain corrupted and finalization has no buffered bytes to flush.
findings.trigger: Append stdout bytes E2 82, append stderr text, then append stdout byte AC. The stdout chunks produce replacement characters instead of one euro sign.
findings.remedy: Decode ordinary chunks with this.decoders[stream].write(chunk), preserving independent decoder state for stdout and stderr.

findings.issue: A chunk supplied with final=true is counted and hashed but silently omitted from the output.
findings.trigger: append('stdout', Buffer.from('done'), true) records four raw bytes while read().output remains empty.
findings.remedy: Pass the optional final chunk to this.decoders[stream].end(chunk), retaining raw-byte accounting exactly once.

findings.issue: Admission still counts only running tasks, so the requested four-slot invariant is not enforced. It also counts confirmed tasks if their status is running, contrary to the status-independent contract.
findings.trigger: Call start five times before any supervisor reports started. Each reserved task has status starting and cleanup pending, so all five calls spawn. Tasks that are stopping or cleanup-unconfirmed likewise fail to occupy slots.
findings.remedy: Count tasks whose cleanup !== "confirmed" instead of tasks whose status === "running". Preserve the closed check and keep rejection before task-map mutation and spawning.

findings.issue: TaskRunner.start counts only running tasks, allowing admission beyond four slots while cleanup remains pending or unconfirmed.
findings.trigger: Start five tasks before their startup acknowledgements arrive, or start another task when four existing tasks include starting, stopping, or cleanup-unconfirmed tasks. The extra start spawns and mutates the task map.
findings.remedy: Replace the admission filter task.status === "running" with task.cleanup !== "confirmed". Keep the closed check and admission guard before task creation, map insertion, and spawning.

findings.issue: VerificationRegistry.resolve captures current inputs but ignores their digest when determining freshness, so a receipt can remain passed after declared files change.
findings.trigger: Record a successful receipt with matching before/after digests, then modify a declared config or source file and resolve the receipt. If capture still succeeds, resolve incorrectly returns passed.
findings.remedy: Require current.digest === receipt.before?.digest && current.digest === receipt.after?.digest for freshness. Preserve the existing stale/failed classification and command-pass conditions.

findings.issue: Freshness ignores the current input digest, so a receipt still reports passed after a declared source or config file changes.
findings.trigger: Capture matching before/after inventories and add a successful command outcome, then change a declared file. resolve captures the changed inventory in current but compares only receipt.before?.digest with receipt.after?.digest. The receipt incorrectly remains passed; an unsuccessful receipt similarly remains failed instead of becoming stale.
findings.remedy: Require current.digest, receipt.before?.digest, and receipt.after?.digest to agree before applying the existing passed/failed outcome predicate. This also rejects missing before/after digests. Preserve the existing stale result when input capture fails.

findings.issue: URL query secrets remain visible; the requested query-parameter redaction is missing.
findings.trigger: redactCommand('curl "https://example.com/path?ToKeN=abc&mode=fast"') retains ToKeN=abc. URL userinfo redaction does not cover queries, and the token checks only match the beginning of whitespace-delimited parts. The same gap affects secret, password, api_key, api-key, and access_token parameters.
findings.remedy: Redact the specified query-parameter values case-insensitively before UTF-8 truncation, preserving the surrounding URL and existing redaction behavior. Cover repeated parameters, mixed case, fragments, and non-secret parameters.

findings.issue: redactCommand does not redact secret URL query parameter values, leaving the requested leak unfixed.
findings.trigger: curl 'https://example.com/path?ToKeN=abc&secret=def&password=ghi&api_key=jkl&api-key=mno&access_token=pqr&mode=safe#section' exposes every secret value.
findings.remedy: Before UTF-8 truncation, redact values of token, secret, password, api_key, api-key and access_token query parameters case-insensitively. Preserve parameter names, query separators, non-secret parameters, fragments and surrounding command text, while retaining the existing redaction passes.

findings.issue: The inclusive comparison reports a nonexistent next page when the final page is full.
findings.trigger: pageInfo(20, 1, 10) returns { hasNext: true, count: 10 }, although both pages exhaust all 20 items.
findings.remedy: Change `total >= (page + 1) * size` to `total > (page + 1) * size`. Preserve the function signature, returned fields, and count calculation.

findings.issue: hasNext is true on a full final page because the boundary comparison includes equality.
findings.trigger: pageInfo(20, 1, 10) returns hasNext: true although no items remain.
findings.remedy: Change total >= (page + 1) * size to total > (page + 1) * size. Leave the API and count calculation unchanged.

findings.issue: The truthiness fallback converts an explicit retry budget of zero to three, enabling retries.
findings.trigger: retryDelay({ retries: 0 }) returns retries: 3.
findings.remedy: Replace `options.retries || 3` with `options.retries ?? 3` to preserve zero while defaulting omitted or null budgets to three, without changing the public API.

findings.issue: An explicit retry budget of zero becomes three, violating the requirement to disable retries.
findings.trigger: retryDelay({ retries: 0 }) returns { retries: 3, delayMs: 100 } because || treats zero as falsy.
findings.remedy: Replace options.retries || 3 with options.retries ?? 3. This preserves zero, defaults omitted or null budgets to three, and preserves the public API.

findings.issue: The requested options-object migration is not implemented. The formatter and both repository callers still use positional currency strings.
findings.trigger: formatAmount(1234, { currency: "EUR" }) returns "[object Object] 12.34". main.mjs:3 and billing/invoice.mjs:3 still pass "EUR" and "GBP" directly.
findings.remedy: Change the signature to formatAmount(cents, { currency = "USD" } = {}) and update both callers to pass { currency: "EUR" } and { currency: "GBP" }, preserving their existing output.

findings.issue: formatAmount still accepts a positional currency instead of an options object.
findings.trigger: formatAmount(1234, { currency: "EUR" }) returns "[object Object] 12.34".
findings.remedy: Change the signature to formatAmount(cents, { currency = "USD" } = {}).

findings.issue: cartTotal still passes currency positionally.
findings.trigger: After migrating the formatter, cartTotal(1234) would return "USD 12.34" instead of "EUR 12.34".
findings.remedy: Call formatAmount(cents, { currency: "EUR" }).

findings.issue: invoiceTotal still passes currency positionally.
findings.trigger: After migrating the formatter, invoiceTotal(1234) would return "USD 12.34" instead of "GBP 12.34".
findings.remedy: Call formatAmount(cents, { currency: "GBP" }).

findings.issue: Prefix matching incorrectly includes sibling directories whose names begin with the root name.
findings.trigger: isWithin('/app', '/application') returns true.
findings.remedy: Return root === '/' || candidate === root || candidate.startsWith(root + '/'); this includes the root and descendants while excluding prefix-sharing siblings under the supported absolute normalized POSIX contract.

findings.issue: The prefix check includes sibling directories, so the requested fix is absent.
findings.trigger: isWithin('/app', '/application') returns true, although '/application' is outside '/app'.
findings.remedy: Use candidate === root || candidate.startsWith(root === '/' ? '/' : root + '/') to enforce directory boundaries while preserving root equality and descendants of '/'.

findings.issue: receiptFresh ignores inputs, so receipts remain fresh after declared source, test, or config bytes change.
findings.trigger: With the same head, inputs {"main.mjs":"old"} and {"main.mjs":"new"} return true. Added or removed paths also go undetected.
findings.remedy: Require equal heads, identical own input-key sets, and exact string equality for each corresponding value. Compare keys independently of insertion order.

findings.issue: receiptFresh compares only head, so changed input bytes or added/deleted input paths incorrectly leave receipts fresh.
findings.trigger: before.head equals after.head but their inputs differ in any path or string value.
findings.remedy: Keep the head comparison and require identical own input key sets and exact string values for each key. Compare keys without depending on insertion order.

findings.issue: The name is only displayed in memory; it is neither persisted nor restored after reload.
findings.trigger: Save a name and reload the page: the saved name disappears.
findings.remedy: Store accepted names in localStorage and read that same key on page load to restore the saved display using textContent.

findings.issue: Submissions retain surrounding whitespace and accept blank names while reporting success.
findings.trigger: Submit "  Alice  " or a whitespace-only value; whitespace is retained or the saved display is cleared and "Saved" appears.
findings.remedy: Trim the input value and return immediately if it is empty, before updating storage, the saved display, or status.

findings.issue: “Saved” is reported without persisting the name, and page initialization never restores it.
findings.trigger: On the fresh origin, submit a name and reload. The name disappears because it exists only in the DOM.
findings.remedy: Store accepted names in localStorage and read the same key on page load. Render restored names with textContent to preserve HTML-character safety.

findings.issue: Submissions are neither trimmed nor checked for blank input.
findings.trigger: Submitting "  Ada  " displays surrounding whitespace. Submitting only spaces replaces an existing displayed name and reports “Saved.”
findings.remedy: Trim the input and return immediately if it is empty, before changing the saved display, storage, or status.

findings.issue: The list still displays raw status codes instead of using the detail view’s shared labels and unknown-status fallback.
findings.trigger: list(["pending", "done", "other"]) returns ["Status: pending", "Status: done", "Status: other"] instead of ["Status: Awaiting review", "Status: Complete", "Status: Unknown"].
findings.remedy: Import statusLabel from ./status.mjs and use statusLabel(value) in the existing map callback.

findings.issue: The list renders raw status codes instead of using the detail view’s shared labels and unknown-status fallback.
findings.trigger: list(["pending", "done", "other"]) returns raw codes instead of "Status: Awaiting review", "Status: Complete", and "Status: Unknown".
findings.remedy: Import statusLabel from "./status.mjs" and replace "Status: " + value with "Status: " + statusLabel(value) in the map callback.

findings.issue: A zero budget returns the entire input, violating the byte bound.
findings.trigger: tailText("abc", 0) uses subarray(-0), which is subarray(0), and returns "abc".
findings.remedy: Return an empty string when budget is zero.

findings.issue: Slicing inside a UTF-8 code point introduces replacement characters and can exceed the byte budget.
findings.trigger: tailText("é", 1) retains only the final continuation byte and decodes it as "�", which occupies three UTF-8 bytes. The required result is empty.
findings.remedy: Clamp the starting byte offset to zero, then advance past any continuation bytes before decoding. This retains the longest suffix of whole code points that fits the budget while preserving the exported function.

findings.issue: A zero budget returns the entire input because subarray(-0) starts at byte zero.
findings.trigger: tailText("abc", 0) returns "abc" instead of "".
findings.remedy: Return "" immediately when budget === 0.

findings.issue: Slicing inside a multibyte code point introduces a replacement character and can exceed the byte budget.
findings.trigger: tailText("é", 1) returns "�" (3 UTF-8 bytes) instead of "".
findings.remedy: Compute start = Math.max(0, bytes.length - budget), then advance start past UTF-8 continuation bytes before decoding bytes.subarray(start). This retains the longest suffix of whole code points.

findings.issue: sortedJobs mutates and returns the input array instead of returning a new array, and can throw when the input is frozen.
findings.trigger: Passing a retained array changes its order; passing a frozen array with multiple jobs can throw a TypeError.
findings.remedy: Copy before sorting: return [...jobs].sort((a, b) => b.priority - a.priority); This preserves job identities, stable ordering for equal priorities, and support for negative and zero priorities.

findings.issue: Sorting in place mutates the caller's array and returns that same array, violating the required new-array contract. Frozen arrays can throw during sorting.
findings.trigger: Passing jobs with priorities [0, 2, -1] reorders the original array. Passing a frozen array containing those jobs throws a TypeError.
findings.remedy: Sort a shallow copy: return [...jobs].sort((a, b) => b.priority - a.priority). This preserves object identity, stable ordering for equal priorities, and support for zero and negative priorities.

findings.issue: Splitting on commas does not parse quoted fields: it retains delimiters and doubled quotes and splits embedded commas into extra fields.
findings.trigger: parseRecord('"a,b","c""d"') returns ['"a', 'b"', '"c""d"'] instead of ['a,b', 'c"d']. Quoted CR/LF text also retains its surrounding quotes.
findings.remedy: Replace split with a stateful scan that recognizes quoted fields, preserves embedded commas and CR/LF, decodes doubled quotes, and preserves empty and trailing fields.

findings.issue: Malformed quoting is accepted instead of rejected.
findings.trigger: Inputs '"abc', 'a"b', and '"a"x' all return arrays despite containing an unterminated quote, a quote inside an unquoted field, or characters after a closing quote.
findings.remedy: During the scan, reject quotes in unquoted fields, require comma/end after closing quotes, and reject end-of-input while a quoted field remains open.

findings.issue: Splitting on commas does not parse quoted fields or decode doubled quotes; enclosing quotes remain in returned text.
findings.trigger: For example, `"a,b","c""d"` should return ["a,b","c\"d"], but produces three incorrectly parsed fields.
findings.remedy: Replace split with a quote-aware scan that removes enclosing quotes, decodes doubled quotes, and preserves commas and CR/LF within quoted fields, along with empty and trailing fields.

findings.issue: Malformed quoting is accepted instead of rejected.
findings.trigger: Inputs such as `"abc` (unterminated), `a"b` (quote in an unquoted field), and `"a"x` (text after a closing quote) all return arrays.
findings.remedy: Track unquoted, quoted, and closed-quote states; reject illegal quotes, any non-comma character after a closing quote, and end-of-input while still quoted.

findings.issue: An invalidated load's success unconditionally caches its stale value and deletes any newer pending entry.
findings.trigger: Start load A, invalidate its key, then start load B. If A resolves while B is pending, subsequent gets receive A's stale value; if A resolves after B succeeds, it overwrites B's cached value.
findings.remedy: In the success handler, set values and delete pending only when pending.get(key) === request. Always return the value to the original callers.

findings.issue: An invalidated load's rejection unconditionally deletes a newer pending entry, breaking in-flight promise sharing.
findings.trigger: Start load A, invalidate its key, start load B, then reject A while B remains pending. The next get starts a third load instead of sharing B's promise.
findings.remedy: In the rejection handler, delete pending only when pending.get(key) === request. Always rethrow the error to the original callers.

findings.issue: Settled loads unconditionally update shared state, allowing invalidated requests to cache stale values or remove newer in-flight entries.
findings.trigger: Call get(key) for request A, invalidate(key), then get(key) for request B. If A resolves, it caches A's stale value and deletes B's pending entry—even if B already resolved and cached its newer value. If A rejects while B is pending, it deletes B's entry, allowing another get to start a duplicate load.
findings.remedy: In both settlement handlers, mutate values and pending only when pending.get(key) === request. Always return the value or rethrow the error so old callers still receive their original result.

findings.issue: The once subscription remains callable until its callback returns, violating at-most-once execution under re-entrancy or exceptions.
findings.trigger: A once callback synchronously emitting the same event invokes itself again, potentially overflowing the stack. If it throws, remove() is skipped and a later emit invokes it again.
findings.remedy: Give the wrapper a fired flag; check and set it, then unsubscribe before invoking the callback. The flag also prevents invocation from an older emit snapshot. Forward arguments and let callback exceptions propagate.

findings.issue: Unsubscribing one registration removes every subscription using the same callback.
findings.trigger: Register the same callback twice with on(), then call either returned unsubscribe function. The filter removes both registrations, so the remaining subscription never runs.
findings.remedy: Give each registration a unique identity and remove only that registration. Preserve emit's snapshot iteration so ordinary removals do not cancel callbacks already captured.

findings.issue: once removes its subscription only after the callback returns, allowing repeated execution during re-entrant emits and leaving it registered if the callback throws.
findings.trigger: A once callback synchronously emits the same event or throws. Also, an earlier listener can trigger a nested emit that consumes the once listener before its outer snapshot entry executes.
findings.remedy: Give each once wrapper a fired flag. Return if already fired; otherwise set it and unsubscribe before invoking the callback. Forward all arguments and let exceptions propagate.

findings.issue: on's unsubscribe function removes every registration of the same callback instead of just its own subscription.
findings.trigger: Register the same callback twice, then invoke either returned unsubscribe function; both subscriptions disappear.
findings.remedy: Store a unique entry per registration and remove only that entry by identity. Continue iterating a snapshot in emit without checking whether ordinary entries remain registered.

findings.issue: Invalid limits are not rejected before work runs.
findings.trigger: An empty input accepts any invalid limit; with nonempty input, zero can loop indefinitely and fractional limits can dispatch work.
findings.remedy: Before processing items, reject unless Number.isInteger(limit) && limit > 0.

findings.issue: work receives a batch-relative index instead of the original input index.
findings.trigger: When items.length > limit, callback indices restart at zero for each batch.
findings.remedy: Map with (item, offset) => work(item, index + offset).

findings.issue: Failure can reject the returned Promise while already-started jobs are still running.
findings.trigger: A job rejects while a batch sibling remains pending, or work throws synchronously after an earlier job in the batch has started.
findings.remedy: Track every started job and the first observed error; stop launching upon observing failure, await settlement of all started jobs, then reject with that error. Catch synchronous throws during dispatch as well.

findings.issue: Invalid limits are not rejected before work runs.
