findings.trigger: With nonempty input, limit 1.5 invokes work, while limit 0 repeatedly processes empty slices without completing. Empty input accepts every invalid limit.
findings.remedy: Before processing input, reject unless Number.isInteger(limit) && limit > 0.

findings.issue: Failure rejects the returned Promise before already-started jobs settle.
findings.trigger: With limit 2, if the first job remains pending and the second rejects, Promise.all rejects immediately. A synchronous throw from the second work call also exits immediately while the first job remains pending; its later rejection may be unhandled.
findings.remedy: Track started jobs and capture synchronous throws and rejections. Stop dispatching once a failure is observed, await settlement of all started jobs, then reject with the first observed error.

findings.issue: Work receives batch-relative indices instead of input indices.
findings.trigger: For three items and limit 2, work receives indices 0, 1, 0 instead of 0, 1, 2 because map runs on each slice.
findings.remedy: Wrap the callback and pass index + batchIndex to work.

findings.issue: The loop permits attempts + 1 operations and an extra sleep instead of treating attempts as the total attempt count.
findings.trigger: With attempts: 1 and an operation that rejects, retry sleeps and invokes operation(1, signal) instead of immediately preserving the first operation error.
findings.remedy: Use index < attempts and rethrow the operation error when index === attempts - 1.

findings.issue: attempts is not validated before work begins.
findings.trigger: attempts: 0 invokes the operation; negative or NaN values silently return undefined; fractional values can exhaust the loop without preserving the final error.
findings.remedy: Before invoking operation or sleep, reject unless Number.isInteger(attempts) && attempts > 0.

findings.issue: Cancellation is never checked, allowing operations after cancellation and successful returns when cancellation must reject.
findings.trigger: An already-aborted signal still reaches operation. If operation aborts the signal and resolves, its value is returned. If sleep resolves after cancellation, another operation runs.
findings.remedy: Check cancellation before each operation, after an operation resolves, and when handling an operation failure before sleeping or rethrowing. Throw signal.reason exactly. Check again after sleep before further work, keeping cancellation checks outside the operation-error catch so cancellation is never retried.

findings.issue: The loop permits attempts + 1 operations instead of attempts total.
findings.trigger: With attempts: 1, a failed operation causes a sleep and a second operation.
findings.remedy: Use index < attempts and rethrow the operation error when index === attempts - 1.

findings.issue: attempts is not validated before work begins.
findings.trigger: Zero, negative, fractional, nonnumeric or infinite attempts can cause invalid execution counts, silent resolution or unbounded retries.
findings.remedy: Before invoking operation or sleep, reject unless Number.isInteger(attempts) && attempts > 0.

findings.issue: Cancellation is never checked or observed by retry itself.
findings.trigger: An already-aborted signal still permits operations; cancellation during sleep can permit another operation; cancellation before an operation resolves can still return success.
findings.remedy: Check signal cancellation before every operation and after operation resolution, rejecting with signal.reason. Observe abort while awaiting sleep so cancellation rejects with signal.reason and prevents further operations, even when injected sleep ignores the signal; clean up any abort listener.

findings.issue: Duplicate target names are accepted and cause store calls before validation.
findings.trigger: Two changes have the same name.
findings.remedy: Check all names for duplicates and reject before calling snapshot or any store method.

findings.issue: Rollback restores only successfully written targets, omitting the failed and not-yet-written targets.
findings.trigger: Any write fails, especially after mutating its target.
findings.remedy: Restore every entry in before in reverse order, using write for originally present targets and remove for originally absent targets. Remove the written tracking and name lookup.

findings.issue: A rollback failure stops remaining restorations and replaces the original write error.
findings.trigger: A restoration write or remove throws.
findings.remedy: Catch each restoration error and continue. Collect errors starting with the original write error, followed by rollback errors in observation order. Throw AggregateError if any restoration failed; otherwise rethrow the original error object.

findings.issue: Duplicate target names are accepted and cause store calls, violating the required validation boundary.
findings.trigger: Two changes with the same name reach snapshot(), which calls store.has/read before any duplicate validation; both writes can then succeed.
findings.remedy: Validate all target names for duplicates before calling snapshot or any store method, and reject duplicates.

findings.issue: Rollback restores only successfully completed writes, leaving the failed and not-yet-written targets unrestored.
findings.trigger: If store.write mutates a target and then throws, its name is never added to written. Rollback skips that target and every later target, violating the requirement to restore ALL targets in reverse order.
findings.remedy: Iterate the complete before snapshot in reverse order, restoring each original value or removing each originally absent target. Remove the written tracking and per-target find lookup.

findings.issue: A rollback failure aborts remaining restorations and replaces the original write error.
findings.trigger: When a restoration write or remove rejects, execution exits the catch block immediately; remaining targets are skipped and no AggregateError is produced.
findings.remedy: Catch each restoration error and continue. After all restorations, throw an AggregateError containing the original write error first and rollback errors in observation order, or rethrow the original error object if rollback succeeded.

findings.issue: Version handling violates the supported interface: unknown or missing versions are accepted, and schema 2 inputs are modified.
findings.trigger: An input without version returns version 2 instead of throwing. A schema 2 input with display.theme set to "light" returns "dark".
findings.remedy: Validate the version, reject anything other than 1 or 2, and return an unchanged deep clone for version 2.

findings.issue: Replacing display discards its unrelated fields and any existing theme when no legacy theme exists.
findings.trigger: A schema 1 input with display: { theme: "light", density: "compact" } loses density and changes theme to "dark".
findings.remedy: Preserve the cloned display object and only overwrite display.theme when an own top-level theme exists.

findings.issue: The truthiness fallback loses an empty legacy theme and invents a theme when none exists.
findings.trigger: theme: "" becomes "dark"; an input without any theme gains display.theme: "dark".
findings.remedy: Check Object.hasOwn(settings, "theme") and copy its exact value without a fallback.

findings.issue: The legacy theme is copied rather than moved.
findings.trigger: Migrating { version: 1, theme: "light" } leaves theme at the top level as well as under display.
findings.remedy: Delete the top-level theme from the cloned schema 1 result after moving it.

findings.issue: The shallow spread shares unrelated nested objects with the input.
findings.trigger: For settings containing plugin: { options: {} }, result.plugin === settings.plugin; modifying the result's plugin data mutates the input.
findings.remedy: Deep-clone the complete JSON input before applying migration changes.

findings.issue: The legacy theme is copied rather than moved; empty strings become "dark", and missing themes invent a value.
findings.trigger: Schema 1 input has an own theme property, an empty-string theme, or no theme property.
findings.remedy: Check Object.hasOwn(settings, "theme"); only when present, assign its exact value to display.theme and delete the cloned top-level theme.

findings.issue: Replacing display discards its unrelated fields and any existing theme when no legacy theme exists.
findings.trigger: Schema 1 input contains display fields such as contrast, or contains display.theme without a top-level theme.
findings.remedy: Preserve the cloned display object and overwrite only its theme when an own legacy theme exists; create display only when needed.

findings.issue: Schema 2 inputs are modified, and missing or unsupported versions are silently accepted.
findings.trigger: Input has version 2, lacks version, or has any version other than 1 or 2.
findings.remedy: Validate the version; reject unsupported or missing versions, return an unchanged deep clone for version 2, and migrate only version 1.

findings.issue: The shallow spread shares nested objects with the input.
findings.trigger: Input includes a nested plugin object, array, or other unrelated object; modifying it through the result also modifies the input.
findings.remedy: Deep-clone the complete input before applying migration changes.

findings.issue: Primitive types collapse to the same string.
findings.trigger: canonicalKey(1) equals canonicalKey("1"); likewise true and "true", or null and "null".
findings.remedy: Serialize primitives with JSON.stringify(value) instead of String(value).

findings.issue: Arrays and objects have no distinct representation.
findings.trigger: canonicalKey([]) equals canonicalKey({}); canonicalKey([1]) equals canonicalKey({"0":1}).
findings.remedy: Handle arrays with Array.isArray, preserving element order, and enclose their canonical elements in brackets; enclose canonical object entries in braces.

findings.issue: Unescaped keys and values and missing nested boundaries cause collisions between different JSON structures.
findings.trigger: {"a":"b,c:d"} and {"a":"b","c":"d"} both produce "a:b,c:d". {"a":{"b":1}} and {"a:b":1} both produce "a:b:1".
findings.remedy: JSON-quote keys and string values and delimit every container. Serialize sorted own object keys directly, avoiding mutation or reconstruction through property assignment so __proto__ remains an ordinary data key.

findings.issue: Primitive types collide because String(value) removes type information.
findings.trigger: 1 and "1" both produce "1"; true and "true", and null and "null", also collide.
findings.remedy: Encode primitives with JSON.stringify(value) to preserve their JSON types.

findings.issue: Arrays and objects have no distinct structural encoding.
findings.trigger: ["x"] and {"0":"x"} both produce "0:x". Empty arrays and empty objects both produce "".
findings.remedy: Handle arrays separately, encoding elements in their original order inside brackets. Encode objects with sorted own keys inside braces.

findings.issue: Unescaped keys and values make entry boundaries ambiguous.
findings.trigger: {"a":"x,b:y"} and {"a":"x","b":"y"} both produce "a:x,b:y". Likewise, {"a:b":"c"} and {"a":"b:c"} collide.
findings.remedy: JSON-quote property names and string values, and use explicit container delimiters around recursively encoded contents.

findings.issue: Empty pages terminate collection even when more pages exist, omitting later items.
findings.trigger: A page returns items: [] and nextCursor: "next"; cursor becomes null and "next" is never fetched.
findings.remedy: Always assign page.nextCursor to cursor and stop only when it is null.

findings.issue: Repeated non-null cursors are fetched again instead of causing rejection, potentially looping forever.
findings.trigger: A nonempty page returns nextCursor: "a", and the page fetched with "a" also returns nextCursor: "a"; collect fetches "a" again.
findings.remedy: Track non-null next cursors in a Set and reject a repeated cursor before issuing its duplicate fetch.

findings.issue: Duplicate IDs retain the last value regardless of revision, violating highest-revision selection and first-value retention on ties.
findings.trigger: For the same ID, revision 2 followed by revision 1 retains revision 1; two distinct values with equal revisions retain the second.
findings.remedy: Build the Map incrementally, inserting unseen IDs and replacing existing values only when the incoming revision is strictly higher. This preserves first occurrence order.

findings.issue: Duplicate IDs always retain the last value, violating highest-revision selection and first-value retention on equal revisions.
findings.trigger: An ID appears again with a lower or equal revision.
findings.remedy: Build the Map incrementally: insert unseen IDs and replace existing values only when the incoming revision is strictly greater. This preserves first occurrence order.

findings.issue: An empty page prematurely ends collection even when it supplies a next cursor.
findings.trigger: A page has items: [] and a non-null nextCursor.
findings.remedy: Assign cursor = page.nextCursor unconditionally and stop only when it is null.

findings.issue: Repeated non-null cursors are not detected, allowing duplicate fetches and potentially infinite loops.
findings.trigger: A page returns a non-null nextCursor that was returned previously.
findings.remedy: Track non-null next cursors in a Set. Reject when one repeats, before fetching it again.

findings.issue: The validator accepts unsafe names that the request requires rejecting, including traversal, Windows paths, control characters, and invalid segments.
findings.remedy: Require a nonempty string; reject leading slash, any backslash, colon, or control character. Remove at most one optional final slash, split on '/', and reject empty segments, '.' or '..', and segments ending in dot or space. Keep Unicode, internal spaces, and literal percent sequences unchanged.

findings.issue: Windows paths and forbidden characters pass validation, violating the cross-platform extraction boundary.
findings.trigger: Inputs such as "C:/outside", "\\\\server\\share", "..\\outside", "a:b", and names containing NUL or control characters return true.
findings.remedy: Reject every backslash, colon, NUL, and control character before validating slash-separated segments. Keep names as raw text; do not URL-decode them.

findings.issue: The substring check does not enforce the required segment rules.
findings.trigger: Empty names, "a//b", "a//", ".", "..", "a/..", "a/./b", "a./b", and "a /b" return true despite being prohibited.
findings.remedy: Require a nonempty name, allow at most one optional final slash, then reject empty segments, dot segments, and segments ending in a dot or space. Preserve Unicode, internal spaces, and literal "%2e%2e".

findings.issue: Decoding each chunk independently corrupts UTF-8 characters split across chunks.
findings.trigger: Writing Buffers [0xC3] and [0xA9, 0x0A] emits replacement characters instead of "é".
findings.remedy: Use a persistent UTF-8 StringDecoder and flush it at end().

findings.issue: Only LF is recognized; CRLF retains CR in the output, and standalone CR never completes a line during write.
findings.trigger: Writing "a\r\nb\rc" emits "a\r" and leaves "b\rc" pending. Splitting CRLF across chunks has the same defect.
findings.remedy: Recognize LF, CRLF, and standalone CR, retaining enough state to count a split CRLF once while preserving empty lines.

findings.issue: end() invents empty lines and is not harmless when repeated.
findings.trigger: end() on a fresh instance emits ""; writing "a\n" then ending emits an extra ""; repeated end() calls keep emitting "".
findings.remedy: Make end() idempotent and emit the final unterminated line only when nonempty, while resolving any pending CR delimiter.

findings.issue: write() accepts input after end() instead of throwing.
findings.trigger: Calling end() followed by write(Buffer.from("a\n")) emits another line without error; even an empty write after end is accepted.
findings.remedy: Track the ended state and check it before processing any write.

findings.issue: Decoding each chunk independently corrupts UTF-8 characters split across chunks.
findings.trigger: Write Buffer.from([0xC3]), then Buffer.from([0xA9, 0x0A]); the emitted line should be "é".
findings.remedy: Use a persistent UTF-8 StringDecoder for writes and flush it during the first end().

findings.issue: Only LF is recognized; CRLF retains the CR and standalone CR does not delimit lines.
findings.trigger: Writing "a\r\nb\rc\n" emits incorrect lines. A CR followed by LF in another chunk must also count once.
findings.remedy: Scan for LF, CRLF and standalone CR, preserving empty lines and retaining a trailing CR until the next nonempty write or end().

findings.issue: end() unconditionally emits, inventing empty lines and making repeated end() observable.
findings.trigger: Call end() on an empty stream, after writing "a\n", or twice after writing "a".
findings.remedy: Make repeated end() return immediately; on the first end(), finish decoding and delimiter processing, then emit only a nonempty unterminated remainder.

findings.issue: write() remains usable after end().
findings.trigger: Call end(), then write any Buffer, including an empty Buffer; no exception is thrown.
findings.remedy: Track the ended state and throw at the beginning of write() when it is set.

findings.issue: The cache key omits tenant and archived and ambiguously joins labels, allowing unrelated requests to share data.
findings.trigger: Different tenants or archived flags with identical labels collide. Labels ['a,b'] and ['a','b'] also collide; [] and [''] collide.
findings.remedy: Key the Map with JSON.stringify([tenant, normalizedLabels, query.archived]), using sorted unique labels.

findings.issue: Normalization mutates caller input, retains duplicate labels, and passes the caller's query to the loader instead of a fresh normalized query.
findings.trigger: Unsorted input is modified; frozen label arrays can throw; ['a','a'] and ['a'] fail to share an entry; fetchReport receives duplicates and caller-owned objects.
findings.remedy: Create labels with [...new Set(query.labels)].sort() and a fresh { labels, archived: query.archived } query. Use those labels for identity and pass the fresh query with the original tenant.

findings.issue: Rejected Promises remain cached indefinitely, preventing retries.
findings.trigger: A load rejects and an equal normalized request is made afterward.
findings.remedy: Attach a rejection handler to the cached Promise that deletes the key only if its current entry is that same Promise, then rethrows the error.

findings.issue: Synchronous fetchReport throws escape synchronously. The cache's Promise.resolve(load(...)) cannot catch them because load is evaluated first.
findings.trigger: fetchReport throws before returning a Promise.
findings.remedy: Return Promise.resolve().then(() => fetchReport(tenant, query)) from requestReport so synchronous throws become rejections.

findings.issue: The cache key omits tenant and archived and conflates distinct label sets, allowing unrelated requests to receive another request's result.
findings.trigger: Requests for different tenants or archived flags with identical labels share an entry. Labels ["a,b"] and ["a","b"] also collide.
findings.remedy: Use a collision-safe key such as JSON.stringify([tenant, normalizedLabels, query.archived]) and retain Map storage.

findings.issue: Normalization mutates caller input, retains duplicate labels, and passes the original query to the loader.
findings.trigger: Sorting ["b","a","a"] changes the caller's array and sends duplicate labels to fetchReport. It also produces a different cache entry from the semantically equal ["a","b"]. A frozen labels array can throw during sorting.
findings.remedy: Create a fresh query with labels: [...new Set(query.labels)].sort() and unchanged archived. Use it for both identity and loading, preserving the original tenant.

findings.issue: Synchronous transport exceptions escape instead of becoming Promise rejections.
findings.trigger: If fetchReport throws synchronously, load throws before Promise.resolve is called, so the report call throws without returning a Promise.
findings.remedy: Invoke the loader inside a Promise continuation, or catch synchronous exceptions and convert them to rejections. Cache and return the same Promise for equivalent requests.

findings.issue: Rejected Promises remain cached permanently, preventing retries.
findings.trigger: After a loader rejection, every equivalent request receives the same rejected Promise without calling fetchReport again.
findings.remedy: Attach rejection handling that deletes the entry only if it still contains that request's Promise, then rethrows the error. Retain fulfilled entries.

findings.issue: The finally block can replace a source exception with an exception from iterator.return, violating exception preservation.
findings.trigger: iterator.next() (or an iterator-result getter) throws, then accessing or calling iterator.return also throws.
findings.remedy: Track whether iteration threw. Still attempt cleanup, but suppress cleanup errors when preserving an existing exception; otherwise propagate cleanup errors.

findings.issue: A cleanup exception can replace the source exception, violating the requirement to preserve source exceptions.
findings.trigger: If iterator.next() throws error A and iterator.return() throws error B, the finally block causes take().next() to throw B instead of A. The same masking occurs for exceptions from item.done or item.value getters.
findings.remedy: Track whether iteration failed and preserve that original exception while still attempting cleanup. Propagate cleanup failures when no iteration exception is pending.

findings.issue: Earlier requests can overwrite results and status owned by the latest submission, including setting Error after a newer request succeeds.
findings.trigger: Submit A, then B; let B complete before A resolves or rejects. A still updates the UI.
findings.remedy: Increment a submission generation on every submit and guard all results/status updates after awaits, including catch, against that generation.

findings.issue: Blank submissions fetch instead of clearing results/status and invalidating pending requests.
findings.trigger: Submit empty or whitespace-only text while results exist or another request is pending.
findings.remedy: After invalidating prior requests, trim the input. If empty, clear only the results container and status, then return without fetching.

findings.issue: Queries are neither trimmed nor URL-encoded, so reserved characters change the requested query.
findings.trigger: Submitting '  cats & dogs#photos  ' introduces an additional URL parameter and fragment instead of sending the intended trimmed query.
findings.remedy: Build the URL using encodeURIComponent on the trimmed nonblank query.

findings.issue: Non-OK HTTP responses can display results and Ready instead of Error.
findings.trigger: A 404 or 500 response contains valid JSON with an items array; fetch resolves and the success path runs.
findings.remedy: Check response.ok and throw on failure before consuming the response as a successful result.

findings.issue: Returned items are interpreted as HTML rather than rendered as text, allowing markup injection.
findings.trigger: An item such as 'example' becomes an element instead of literal text; event-handler markup could execute.
findings.remedy: Create li elements, assign each item's textContent, and replace only the results container's children.

findings.issue: Older requests can overwrite the latest query’s results and status.
findings.trigger: Submit two queries; the earlier request resolves or rejects after the later submission.
findings.remedy: Increment a submission counter on every submit. Capture it per request and update results or status only when it still matches the current counter, including in catch.

findings.issue: Blank submissions fetch instead of clearing results/status and invalidating pending requests.
findings.trigger: Submit empty or whitespace-only text, including while a request is pending.
findings.remedy: After advancing the submission counter, trim the input. If empty, clear results and status and return without fetching.

findings.issue: Nonblank queries are neither trimmed nor URL-encoded.
findings.trigger: Submit text with surrounding whitespace or URL-significant characters such as &, #, or +.
findings.remedy: Build the URL with '/search?q=' + encodeURIComponent(trimmedQuery).

findings.issue: Returned items are interpreted as HTML instead of rendered as text.
findings.trigger: An item contains markup such as 'example' or an HTML event handler.
findings.remedy: Create an li for each item, assign its textContent, and replace only the results list’s children.

findings.issue: Non-OK HTTP responses can incorrectly produce Ready.
findings.trigger: A non-OK response returns valid JSON containing an items array.
findings.remedy: Throw when response.ok is false before reading JSON; let the latest-request-guarded catch display Error.

findings.issue: An unreadable localStorage aborts initialization and prevents the submit handler from being registered.
findings.trigger: Accessing localStorage or calling getItem throws.
findings.remedy: Default to light, attempt the read inside try/catch, and continue initializing the display, selection, and submit handler after a read failure.

findings.issue: Truthy invalid stored values are displayed and leave the select without a valid selection.
findings.trigger: The preference key contains a value other than light or dark, such as blue.
findings.remedy: Accept only light or dark from storage; use light for every other value.

findings.issue: The saved display and status claim success before the write succeeds; a failed write also leaves its exception unhandled.
findings.trigger: setItem throws when the user submits, including when the selection differs from the previously saved value.
findings.remedy: Call setItem with the selected value inside try/catch. Only after success update #saved and show Saved. On failure preserve #saved, show Could not save, and leave the controls usable for retry.

findings.issue: A failed write changes #saved and reports Saved, falsely claiming persistence.
findings.trigger: Select dark and submit when localStorage.setItem throws. The displayed saved value becomes dark and status becomes Saved despite the failure.
findings.remedy: Call setItem inside try/catch before updating #saved. On success, update #saved and show Saved. On failure, preserve #saved, show Could not save, and keep controls usable for retry.

findings.issue: Unreadable storage aborts initialization and prevents the submit handler from being registered.
findings.trigger: Accessing localStorage or calling getItem throws. The saved display remains empty and the form cannot perform the required save/retry behavior.
findings.remedy: Initialize the restored value to light and guard storage access with try/catch. Continue initializing the display, selection, and submit handler after a read failure.

findings.issue: Truthy invalid stored values are restored instead of falling back to light.
findings.trigger: The preference key contains blue. #saved displays blue and the select has no matching option.
findings.remedy: Accept only light or dark from storage; use light for every other value while preserving the preference key.

findings.issue: Normal appends bypass the per-stream StringDecoders, so split UTF-8 characters remain corrupted. Finalization ends decoders that never received bytes.
findings.trigger: Append stdout bytes [0xE2], append stderr text, then append stdout bytes [0x82, 0xAC]. Each stdout chunk is decoded separately into replacement characters instead of producing €; finalization cannot recover it.
findings.remedy: Decode normal chunks with this.decoders[stream].write(chunk) and flush that decoder on finalization. Preserve raw-byte hashing/counting before decoding and the existing tail, cursor, and escaping logic.

findings.issue: OutputRing.append decodes each chunk independently, leaving the per-stream StringDecoders unused and corrupting split UTF-8 characters.
findings.trigger: Append stdout bytes E2 82, then stderr text, then stdout byte AC. The stdout euro sign becomes replacement characters; finalization cannot recover it.
findings.remedy: Replace chunk.toString("utf8") with this.decoders[stream].write(chunk), preserving raw-byte accounting and existing tail/cursor logic.

findings.issue: Finalization silently discards a supplied final chunk from displayed output while including it in byte counts and digests.
findings.trigger: append("stdout", Buffer.from("last"), true) hashes and counts "last" but emits none of it.
findings.remedy: Pass chunk to this.decoders[stream].end(chunk) in the final branch, supporting both a final chunk and the existing undefined-chunk flush.

findings.issue: TaskRunner.start counts only running tasks, allowing tasks without confirmed cleanup to exceed the four-slot limit.
findings.trigger: A fifth start is admitted when existing tasks are starting, stopping, or cleanup-unconfirmed instead of running.
findings.remedy: Replace the admission filter predicate `task.status === "running"` with `task.cleanup !== "confirmed"`. Keep the closed check and rejection before task creation, map insertion, and spawning.

findings.issue: Admission counts only running tasks, so tasks awaiting startup or cleanup do not occupy slots. This leaves the requested four-slot invariant unenforced.
findings.trigger: Call start five times before any supervisor reports started: each existing task has status starting and cleanup pending, so all five spawn. Similarly, stopping and cleanup-unconfirmed tasks are excluded, allowing new starts despite unresolved cleanup.
findings.remedy: Count tasks whose cleanup !== "confirmed" instead of tasks whose status === "running". Keep the closed-runner check and admission rejection before task-map insertion and spawning.

findings.issue: Freshness ignores the newly captured current digest, so changing a declared file after verification still yields passed when the command succeeded. Missing before and after digests also compare equal.
findings.trigger: Record matching before/after snapshots and a successful outcome, then change a declared source or config file. captureInputs reads the changed contents, but fresh compares only receipt.before?.digest with receipt.after?.digest. list inherits this defect through resolve.
findings.remedy: Require current.digest === receipt.before?.digest and current.digest === receipt.after?.digest. Preserve the existing stale precedence, command-success predicate, and fail-closed capture error handling.

findings.issue: VerificationRegistry.resolve captures current inputs but ignores their digest. Matching stored before/after digests can therefore produce a false passed result after declared inputs change; two missing stored digests also compare equal.
findings.trigger: Record a successful receipt with matching before/after digests, then modify a declared source or config file and resolve the receipt. It still reports passed.
findings.remedy: Require all three digests to agree: current.digest === receipt.before?.digest && current.digest === receipt.after?.digest. Preserve the existing stale/failed classification and command-success checks.

findings.issue: redactCommand does not redact URL query parameter secrets, leaving the requested fix unimplemented.
findings.trigger: A command such as curl 'https://example.com/path?ToKeN=secret123&mode=fast' exposes secret123. The same applies to secret, password, api_key, api-key and access_token parameters.
findings.remedy: Add case-insensitive redaction of those exact URL query parameter values before truncation, preserving parameter names, separators, fragments and non-secret URL content. Retain the existing redaction passes and UTF-8 truncation.

findings.issue: redactCommand does not redact URL query secrets, leaving the requested vulnerability unresolved.
findings.trigger: Calling redactCommand('curl "https://example.com/path?token=abc&SECRET=def&Password=ghi&api_key=jkl&api-key=mno&access_token=pqr&view=full"') returns all six secret values unchanged. The existing matchers handle flags, assignments, headers, and userinfo, but none matches query parameters inside URLs.
findings.remedy: Add case-insensitive redaction of the specified query parameter values before UTF-8 truncation, preserving surrounding URL content and existing redaction behavior. Verify mixed-case names, multiple parameters, harmless parameters, and byte limits of at least 32.

findings.issue: hasNext is true for a full final page, offering a nonexistent next page.
findings.trigger: pageInfo(10, 0, 10) returns hasNext: true because total equals (page + 1) * size.
findings.remedy: Change >= to > in hasNext. Keep the function signature and count calculation unchanged; empty lists with positive page sizes still return hasNext: false and count: 0.

findings.issue: hasNext remains true on a full final page, so the requested fix is missing.
findings.trigger: pageInfo(20, 1, 10) returns { hasNext: true, count: 10 }, although no items remain for another page.
findings.remedy: Change the hasNext comparison from >= to >. Preserve the function signature, returned fields, and count calculation; an empty list with a positive size will still return { hasNext: false, count: 0 }.

findings.issue: An explicit retry budget of zero becomes three, so retries are not disabled as requested.
findings.trigger: retryDelay({ retries: 0 }) returns { retries: 3, delayMs: 100 } because || treats zero as falsy.
findings.remedy: Replace options.retries || 3 with options.retries ?? 3. This preserves zero, defaults omitted or null budgets to three, and preserves the public API.

findings.issue: The || fallback replaces an explicit retry budget of zero with three, so retries remain enabled.
findings.trigger: retryDelay({ retries: 0 }) returns retries: 3 instead of retries: 0.
findings.remedy: Replace options.retries || 3 with options.retries ?? 3. This preserves zero and defaults omitted or null budgets to three without changing the public API.

findings.issue: formatAmount still accepts a positional currency rather than the requested options object.
findings.trigger: formatAmount(1234, { currency: "EUR" }) returns "[object Object] 12.34".
findings.remedy: Change the signature to formatAmount(cents, { currency = "USD" } = {}).

findings.issue: cartTotal still passes currency positionally.
findings.trigger: After migrating the formatter, cartTotal(1234) would return "USD 12.34" instead of "EUR 12.34".
findings.remedy: Use formatAmount(cents, { currency: "EUR" }).

findings.issue: invoiceTotal still passes currency positionally.
findings.trigger: After migrating the formatter, invoiceTotal(1234) would return "USD 12.34" instead of "GBP 12.34".
findings.remedy: Use formatAmount(cents, { currency: "GBP" }).

findings.issue: The requested migration is missing: formatAmount still accepts a positional currency, and both repository callers still pass strings.
findings.trigger: formatAmount(1234, { currency: "EUR" }) returns "[object Object] 12.34" instead of "EUR 12.34". main.mjs:3 and billing/invoice.mjs:3 retain the old interface.
findings.remedy: Change the signature to formatAmount(cents, { currency = "USD" } = {}), then update cartTotal to pass { currency: "EUR" } and invoiceTotal to pass { currency: "GBP" }. Preserve their existing formatted output; positional compatibility is unnecessary.

findings.issue: The prefix check includes sibling directories whose names begin with the root name, violating the requested boundary.
findings.trigger: isWithin('/app', '/application') returns true; it must return false.
findings.remedy: Use root === '/' || candidate === root || candidate.startsWith(root + '/'). This preserves root equality and descendants, including the '/' root, within the stated input contract.

findings.issue: The prefix check includes sibling directories whose names begin with the root name.
findings.trigger: isWithin('/app', '/application') returns true.
findings.remedy: Return candidate === root || candidate.startsWith(root === '/' ? '/' : root + '/'). This preserves root equality, descendants, and '/' support within the existing input contract.

findings.issue: receiptFresh compares only head, so it treats receipts with different declared input paths or contents as fresh.
findings.trigger: HEAD remains unchanged while any input is added, removed, renamed, or its UTF-8 content changes.
findings.remedy: Keep the head comparison and also require identical own input key sets and strictly equal string values for every key. Compare keys without relying on insertion order.

findings.issue: receiptFresh ignores inputs, so changed source, test, or config contents incorrectly leave a receipt fresh.
findings.trigger: With the same head, inputs {"main.mjs":"old"} and {"main.mjs":"new"} return true. Added or removed input paths are also ignored.
findings.remedy: Require equal heads, equal own input-key sets, and identical string values for every key. Compare keys independently of insertion order.

findings.issue: The form reports “Saved” without persisting the name, and page load never restores it.
findings.trigger: On the fresh origin, submit a name and reload. The name disappears because the handler only updates textContent.
findings.remedy: Store accepted names in localStorage and read the same key on page load to restore the displayed name. Report success after storage succeeds.

findings.issue: Submissions are neither trimmed nor checked for blank input.
findings.trigger: Submitting "  Alice  " displays surrounding whitespace; submitting whitespace alone replaces the existing name and reports “Saved”.
findings.remedy: Trim the input and return immediately if it is empty before changing storage, the displayed name, or success status. Keep using textContent for safe rendering.

findings.issue: Submitting only updates the DOM; the name is neither persisted nor restored on page load.
findings.trigger: Save a name, then reload the page. The saved name disappears despite the “Saved” status.
findings.remedy: Store accepted names in localStorage under a consistent key and read that key on module initialization to restore the displayed name using textContent.

findings.issue: Submissions preserve surrounding whitespace and accept blank names.
findings.trigger: Submit “  Ada  ” or a whitespace-only value. Whitespace is retained, and blank submissions replace the displayed name and report “Saved”.
findings.remedy: Trim the input value and return immediately if it is empty, before updating storage, displayed text, or status. Use the trimmed value for accepted submissions.

findings.issue: The list still displays raw status codes instead of using the detail view’s shared labels and unknown-status fallback.
findings.trigger: list(["pending", "done", "other"]) returns raw values instead of "Status: Awaiting review", "Status: Complete", and "Status: Unknown".
findings.remedy: Import statusLabel from "./status.mjs" and replace value with statusLabel(value) in the map callback.

findings.issue: The list still renders raw status codes instead of using the detail view’s labels and unknown-status fallback.
findings.trigger: list(["pending", "done", "other"]) returns ["Status: pending", "Status: done", "Status: other"] instead of ["Status: Awaiting review", "Status: Complete", "Status: Unknown"].
findings.remedy: Import statusLabel from ./status.mjs and use "Status: " + statusLabel(value) in the existing map callback.

findings.issue: A zero budget returns the entire text because subarray(-0) equals subarray(0).
findings.trigger: tailText("abc", 0) returns "abc" instead of "".
findings.remedy: Return "" immediately when budget is zero.

findings.issue: Slicing inside a multibyte code point introduces replacement characters and can exceed the byte budget.
findings.trigger: tailText("é", 1) returns "�" (3 UTF-8 bytes) instead of "".
findings.remedy: Compute start = Math.max(0, buffer.length - budget), advance start past UTF-8 continuation bytes, then decode buffer.subarray(start). This preserves the longest suffix of whole code points.

findings.issue: Cutting inside a multibyte code point introduces a replacement character and can exceed the byte budget.
findings.trigger: tailText("é", 1) returns "�", which occupies 3 UTF-8 bytes. The required result is "".
findings.remedy: Compute the byte cutoff, advance past any UTF-8 continuation bytes to the next code-point boundary, and decode the remaining suffix.

findings.issue: A zero-byte budget returns the entire input.
findings.trigger: tailText("abc", 0) returns "abc" because subarray(-0) is subarray(0), violating the zero-byte bound.
findings.remedy: Return "" explicitly when budget is zero.

findings.issue: Array.sort mutates and returns the input array, violating both the non-mutation and new-array requirements. Sorting a frozen array with multiple jobs can throw a TypeError.
findings.trigger: Call sortedJobs with a retained array containing priorities 0 and -1 in ascending order; the caller's array is reordered and the returned array has the same identity. Freeze that array before calling and sorting throws.
findings.remedy: Copy before sorting: return [...jobs].sort((a, b) => b.priority - a.priority); This preserves job identity, descending numeric order, and stable ordering for equal priorities.

findings.issue: sortedJobs sorts the input in place and returns that same array, violating the nonmutation and new-array requirements.
findings.trigger: An unsorted input is reordered for callers retaining it; a frozen array with multiple jobs throws during sorting. Even an empty input returns the original array.
findings.remedy: Copy before sorting: return [...jobs].sort((a, b) => b.priority - a.priority); This preserves job identity, stable ties, and descending numeric order including negative and zero priorities.

findings.issue: Splitting on commas does not parse quoted fields: it splits embedded commas and preserves enclosing and doubled quotes instead of decoding them.
findings.trigger: Inputs such as `"a,b",c`, `"a"`, or `"a""b"` produce incorrect field values.
findings.remedy: Replace split with a character scan that tracks quoted fields, treats commas as separators only outside quotes, removes enclosing quotes, and decodes doubled quotes while preserving all other text, including CR/LF and empty fields.

findings.issue: Malformed quoting is accepted instead of rejected.
findings.trigger: Unterminated quotes (`"abc`), quotes inside unquoted fields (`a"b`), or characters after a closing quote (`"a"x`) return arrays instead of failing.
findings.remedy: In the parser scan, reject quotes within unquoted fields, require comma/end after a closing quote, and reject end-of-input while still inside a quoted field.

findings.issue: Splitting on commas does not parse quoted fields or decode doubled quotes.
findings.trigger: For `"a,b","c""d"`, returns four fragments instead of the two fields `a,b` and `c"d`. Even `"abc"` retains its surrounding quotes.
findings.remedy: Replace split with a quote-aware scan that removes enclosing quotes, decodes doubled quotes, and preserves commas and CR/LF within quoted fields, including empty and trailing fields.

findings.issue: Malformed quoting is accepted instead of rejected.
findings.trigger: Inputs `"abc`, `ab"cd`, and `"abc"x` all return arrays despite violating the required quoting rules.
findings.remedy: During scanning, reject quotes inside unquoted fields, require comma/end after a closing quote, and reject end-of-input within an unterminated quoted field.

findings.issue: Invalidated loads still mutate shared state when they settle. An old success can cache stale data and delete a newer pending entry; an old rejection can also delete that newer entry, allowing duplicate loads.
findings.trigger: Start get(key) as A, invalidate(key), then start get(key) as B. If A resolves while B is pending, subsequent gets return A's stale value. If A rejects while B is pending, subsequent gets start another load instead of sharing B. If A resolves after B succeeds, A overwrites B's cached value.
findings.remedy: In both settlement handlers, mutate values and pending only when pending.get(key) === request. Always return the resolved value or rethrow the error so old callers retain their original result.

findings.issue: Settlement handlers unconditionally modify cache state. An invalidated load can cache a stale value, overwrite a newer value, or delete a newer in-flight entry on either resolution or rejection.
findings.trigger: Start load A, invalidate its key, then start load B for that key. If A settles, it can remove B from pending; if A resolves, it also caches its obsolete result. A can also repopulate the cache after invalidation without B being started.
findings.remedy: Guard both settlement handlers with `pending.get(key) === request`. Only the current request may write to values or delete from pending. Keep returning the value or throwing the error outside the guard so old callers still receive their original outcome.

findings.issue: once removes its subscription after invoking the callback and has no invocation guard, so it can run repeatedly and remains registered if the callback throws.
findings.trigger: The callback synchronously emits the same event or throws. A nested emit from an earlier listener can also invoke the once wrapper before the outer snapshot reaches it.
findings.remedy: Give each once wrapper a fired flag. Return if already fired; otherwise set the flag and remove the subscription before invoking the callback. Forward arguments and let exceptions propagate.

findings.issue: on's unsubscribe function removes every subscription sharing the callback instead of only its own.
findings.trigger: Register the same callback twice, then call either returned unsubscribe function; both subscriptions are removed.
findings.remedy: Store a unique entry per registration and unsubscribe by entry identity. Continue invoking all entries in emit's initial snapshot, including ordinary subscriptions removed during that emit.

findings.issue: A once listener remains eligible while its callback runs, so re-entrant emits invoke it again. A thrown callback also prevents removal.
findings.trigger: A once callback synchronously emits the same event, causing repeated invocation or stack overflow. Alternatively, it throws; after the caller catches the exception, a later emit invokes it again.
findings.remedy: Give each once subscription a fired flag. Check and set it, then unsubscribe before invoking the callback with its arguments. The flag must also suppress invocation from an older emit snapshot after a nested emit has fired it. Let callback exceptions propagate.

findings.issue: The unsubscribe function removes every registration of the same callback instead of only its own subscription.
findings.trigger: Register the same callback twice with on, then call either returned unsubscribe function. The next emit invokes neither subscription, although one should remain.
findings.remedy: Store a unique entry for each registration and remove by entry identity. Continue iterating an emit-start snapshot without checking ordinary entries for current membership, preserving removal-during-emit behavior.

findings.issue: Invalid limits are not rejected before work runs. Zero or negative limits can cause an infinite loop, and empty input accepts every invalid limit.
findings.trigger: mapLimit([1], 0, work) loops without advancing; mapLimit([], 0, work) resolves to [].
findings.remedy: Before processing items, reject unless Number.isInteger(limit) && limit > 0.

findings.issue: The callback receives a batch-relative index instead of the item's input index.
findings.trigger: With items ['a', 'b', 'c'] and limit 2, work receives indices 0, 1, 0 instead of 0, 1, 2.
findings.remedy: Wrap the callback and pass the absolute index: work(item, index + offset).

findings.issue: Failures reject the returned Promise before already-started jobs settle. A synchronous callback throw can also leave earlier promises without rejection handlers because Promise.all is never reached.
findings.trigger: With limit 2, if the first job remains pending and the second throws or rejects, mapLimit rejects immediately while the first job is still running.
findings.remedy: Track started jobs and attach rejection handlers immediately. Record the first observed error, stop dispatch after observing it, await settlement of all started jobs, then reject with that recorded error.

findings.issue: The limit is not validated before work runs or empty input succeeds.
findings.trigger: An invalid limit with empty input returns []; with nonempty input, zero can loop forever and fractional limits can dispatch incorrect batches.
findings.remedy: At function entry, throw unless Number.isInteger(limit) && limit > 0.

findings.issue: work receives the index within each batch rather than the original input index.
findings.trigger: With three items and limit 2, the third item receives index 0 instead of 2.
findings.remedy: Wrap the map callback as (item, offset) => work(item, index + offset).

findings.issue: A synchronous throw or Promise.all rejection rejects the returned Promise without waiting for every already-started job to settle.
findings.trigger: One job fails while another job in the same batch is still pending.
findings.remedy: Track started jobs and capture the first observed failure. Stop dispatching when failure is observed, await settlement of all started jobs, then throw the captured error; catch synchronous throws during dispatch so remaining batch items are not launched.

findings.issue: The loop allows attempts + 1 operations and an extra sleep; the requested final operation error is retried instead of preserved.
findings.trigger: All operations fail with a valid attempts value.
findings.remedy: Use index < attempts and rethrow when index === attempts - 1.

findings.issue: attempts is never validated before work begins.
findings.trigger: attempts is zero, negative, fractional, nonnumeric, or infinite.
findings.remedy: Before invoking operation or sleep, reject unless Number.isInteger(attempts) && attempts > 0.

findings.issue: Cancellation is never checked or observed, so an aborted call can execute operations or return success instead of rejecting with signal.reason.
findings.trigger: The signal is aborted before starting, during sleep, or before an operation's resolution is handled.
findings.remedy: Check cancellation before every operation and after operation success, outside the retryable-error catch. Observe cancellation while awaiting sleep, rejecting with signal.reason and preventing further operations; remove any abort listener when waiting ends. Keep sleep rejection terminal and add no timers.

findings.issue: The loop permits attempts + 1 operations and an extra sleep, violating the total attempt count and losing the intended final operation error.
findings.trigger: With attempts: 1, the first operation rejects; retry sleeps and invokes operation(1, signal) instead of preserving the first error.
findings.remedy: Loop while index < attempts and rethrow the operation error when index === attempts - 1.

findings.issue: attempts is never validated before work begins.
findings.trigger: attempts: 0 invokes the operation; fractional or string values are accepted; Infinity can retry indefinitely.
findings.remedy: Before invoking operation or sleep, reject unless Number.isInteger(attempts) && attempts > 0.

findings.issue: Cancellation is never checked, so passing signal to dependencies does not enforce the required cancellation behavior.
findings.trigger: An already-aborted signal still allows an operation. If an operation aborts the signal and resolves, retry returns success. If sleep resolves after cancellation, another operation starts. A sleep rejection can also propagate a value other than signal.reason after cancellation.
findings.remedy: Check cancellation before starting operations and after awaited operations and sleeps, rejecting with signal.reason. Ensure cancellation on failure paths prevents retries and that cancellation during sleep terminates with signal.reason; preserve terminal sleep rejection when no cancellation occurred.

findings.issue: Duplicate target names are accepted and trigger store calls, violating the requirement to reject duplicates before any store call.
findings.trigger: Two changes with the same name reach snapshot(), which calls has/read, and then both writes execute.
findings.remedy: Validate all target names for duplicates before calling snapshot; reject if any repeat.

findings.issue: Rollback restores only successfully written targets, leaving the failed and not-yet-written targets unrestored.
findings.trigger: A write mutates its target and then throws. Its name never enters written, so its mutation survives rollback. Later targets are also skipped despite the requirement to restore every target.
findings.remedy: Remove written tracking and restore every entry in before in reverse order, using write for original values and remove for original absence.

findings.issue: A rollback failure stops remaining restorations and replaces the original write error instead of producing the required AggregateError.
findings.trigger: Any restoration write/remove rejects; the rollback loop exits immediately and that rejection escapes.
findings.remedy: Catch each restoration error and continue. After all restorations, throw an AggregateError containing the original write error first and rollback errors in observation order; if none occurred, rethrow the original error object.

findings.issue: Duplicate target names are accepted and cause store calls, violating validation requirements.
findings.trigger: changes contains two entries with the same name.
findings.remedy: Validate all names for duplicates before calling snapshot; reject immediately if any repeat.

findings.issue: Rollback restores only successfully written targets, omitting the failed target and targets not yet written.
findings.trigger: Any write fails, especially after mutating its target.
findings.remedy: Restore every entry in before in reverse order, using write for originally existing targets and remove for originally absent targets. Remove the written tracking array and name lookup.

findings.issue: A rollback failure stops remaining restorations and replaces the original write error.
findings.trigger: A write fails and a subsequent rollback write or remove also fails.
findings.remedy: Catch each restoration error and continue restoring. Collect errors starting with the original write error, then rollback errors in observation order; throw AggregateError if rollback failed, otherwise rethrow the original error object.

findings.issue: Theme migration loses empty strings, invents absent themes, and retains the legacy property.
findings.trigger: A schema 1 input has theme: "", lacks an own theme property, or contains any legacy theme.
findings.remedy: Check Object.hasOwn(settings, "theme"); when present, assign its exact value to display.theme and delete the cloned top-level theme. Otherwise leave theme absent or preserve the existing display.theme.

findings.issue: Replacing display discards its unrelated fields and existing theme.
findings.trigger: A schema 1 input contains display fields that should survive migration.
findings.remedy: Preserve the cloned display object, creating it only when needed to move a legacy theme.

findings.issue: The shallow spread shares nested objects with the input.
findings.trigger: An input contains nested unrelated properties, such as plugin objects.
findings.remedy: Deep-clone the entire input before making migration changes.

findings.issue: Schema 2 inputs are modified instead of returned unchanged.
findings.trigger: A version: 2 input has an existing display or no display.
findings.remedy: Return an independent deep clone immediately for version 2.

findings.issue: Missing and unsupported versions are silently converted to version 2.
findings.trigger: The input lacks version or its value is anything other than numeric 1 or 2.
findings.remedy: Validate the version and throw for unsupported or missing values.

findings.issue: Rebuilding display discards all unrelated display fields.
findings.trigger: A schema 1 input with display: { scale: 2 } loses scale after migration.
findings.remedy: Preserve display's existing fields and overwrite only display.theme when an own legacy theme exists.

findings.issue: Legacy theme handling substitutes defaults, ignores property presence, and leaves the top-level theme behind.
findings.trigger: theme: "" becomes "dark"; an absent theme invents "dark"; any existing top-level theme remains in the result.
findings.remedy: Check for an own theme property, copy its exact value to display.theme, and delete the cloned top-level property. When absent, leave display unchanged.

findings.issue: The function accepts missing or unknown versions and rewrites schema 2 inputs.
findings.trigger: Inputs with version: 3 or no version return successfully. A schema 2 input with display.theme: "light" is changed to "dark".
findings.remedy: Validate the version. Return an unchanged deep clone for schema 2, migrate only schema 1, and reject all other versions.

findings.issue: The shallow spread shares nested objects with the input.
findings.trigger: For an input containing plugin: { options: {} }, result.plugin and its options are the original objects; modifying them changes the input.
findings.remedy: Deep-clone the complete JSON input before applying migration changes.

findings.issue: Primitive types collide because String(value) discards type information.
findings.trigger: canonicalKey(1) equals canonicalKey("1"); likewise true and "true", or null and "null".
findings.remedy: Use JSON.stringify(value) for primitive JSON values to preserve types and escape strings.

findings.issue: Arrays and objects share the same encoding, violating their required distinction.
findings.trigger: canonicalKey([1, 2]) equals canonicalKey({"0": 1, "1": 2}); empty arrays and empty objects also collide.
findings.remedy: Handle arrays separately in element order with square-bracket delimiters; encode sorted object entries with curly-brace delimiters.

findings.issue: Unescaped keys and unbounded nested objects create ambiguous key/value boundaries.
findings.trigger: canonicalKey({"a:b": 1}) equals canonicalKey({a: {b: 1}}): both produce "a:b:1".
findings.remedy: JSON-quote every property name and delimit each nested container. Serialize sorted own keys directly, preserving ordinary data keys such as __proto__.

findings.issue: Arrays and objects produce identical keys.
findings.trigger: canonicalKey([1]) equals canonicalKey({"0":1}); [] and {} also collide.
findings.remedy: Handle arrays separately, preserving element order, and use distinct array and object delimiters.

findings.issue: String conversion loses primitive type distinctions.
findings.trigger: 1 and "1", true and "true", and null and "null" each produce identical keys.
findings.remedy: Serialize primitives with JSON.stringify instead of String.

findings.issue: Unescaped property names allow ambiguous entry boundaries.
findings.trigger: {"a":1,"b":2} and {"a:1,b":2} both produce "a:1,b:2".
findings.remedy: Encode property names with JSON.stringify and delimit containers, while recursively sorting object keys. Serialize own keys directly so __proto__ remains ordinary data.

findings.issue: Duplicate IDs always retain the last item, ignoring revision and equal-revision precedence.
findings.trigger: A later item has the same ID and a lower or equal revision.
findings.remedy: Build the Map incrementally; insert unseen IDs and replace existing values only when the incoming revision is strictly greater. Map insertion order preserves first occurrence order.

findings.issue: An empty page terminates collection even when another cursor exists.
findings.trigger: A page has empty items and a non-null nextCursor.
findings.remedy: Assign cursor = page.nextCursor unconditionally and stop only when it is null.

findings.issue: Repeated non-null cursors are fetched again instead of causing rejection, potentially looping forever.
findings.trigger: A page returns a non-null nextCursor already returned by an earlier page.
findings.remedy: Track non-null next cursors in a Set. Reject a repeated cursor before fetching it again; otherwise record it and continue.

findings.issue: Empty pages terminate collection even when nextCursor is non-null, dropping subsequent items.
findings.trigger: The initial page returns { items: [], nextCursor: "a" }; collect stops without fetching "a".
findings.remedy: Assign cursor from page.nextCursor regardless of item count, and stop only when it is null.

findings.issue: Repeated non-null cursors are not detected, allowing duplicate fetches and potentially an infinite loop.
findings.trigger: The initial page points to "a", and the nonempty page fetched at "a" also points to "a"; collect fetches "a" again instead of rejecting.
findings.remedy: Track non-null cursors and reject a repeated nextCursor before issuing its fetch.

findings.issue: Duplicate IDs retain the last value regardless of revision, violating both highest-revision selection and first-value retention on ties.
findings.trigger: Items with the same ID and revisions 2 then 1 retain revision 1. Two distinct values with equal revisions retain the second value.
findings.remedy: Iterate into a Map, inserting unseen IDs and replacing existing values only when the incoming revision is strictly higher. This preserves first occurrence order.

findings.issue: The check accepts invalid archive names, including paths that can escape the extraction directory on Windows.
findings.trigger: Accepted examples include the empty string, '..', 'a/..', 'a/./b', 'a//b', 'C:/file', 'C:file', '..\file', '\\server\share', 'a:b', names containing NUL or controls, and segments ending in a dot or space.
findings.remedy: Validate a nonempty string; reject leading '/', every backslash, colon, and control character. Split on '/', permit only one optional final empty segment for a trailing slash, and reject remaining empty segments, '.' or '..', and segments ending in a dot or space. Preserve Unicode, ordinary internal spaces, and literal percent sequences without URL decoding.

findings.issue: safeEntry accepts unsafe or malformed names because its checks do not enforce the required segment and character rules.
findings.trigger: Examples incorrectly accepted: "", "..", ".", "a/..", "a/./b", "a//b", "a//", "C:/file", "a:b", "a\\b", "\\\\server\\share", names containing NUL or other control characters, and "file." or "file ".
findings.remedy: Require a nonempty string; reject backslashes, colons and control characters. Remove at most one optional final slash, then split on '/'; reject empty segments, '.' or '..', and segments ending in a dot or space. Empty-segment validation also rejects leading slashes. Preserve Unicode, spaces within segments and literal percent sequences without URL-decoding.

findings.issue: Decoding each chunk independently corrupts UTF-8 characters split across chunks.
findings.trigger: Write a multibyte character in two Buffer chunks.
findings.remedy: Use a persistent UTF-8 StringDecoder; process decoder.write(chunk) during writes and decoder.end() during end.

findings.issue: Only LF is recognized: CRLF retains CR in the emitted line, and standalone CR never terminates a line.
findings.trigger: Write "a\r\nb", "a\rb", or CR and LF in separate chunks.
findings.remedy: Scan for LF and CR, preserve empty lines, and track CR across chunks so a following LF does not emit another line. Empty writes must preserve that state.

findings.issue: end() emits an unwanted empty line for an empty stream, after a delimiter, and on repeated calls.
findings.trigger: Call end() without writes, after writing "a\n", or twice after writing "a".
findings.remedy: Make end() idempotent with an ended flag, finalize decoding and pending delimiters, and emit remaining unterminated text only if nonempty.

findings.issue: Writes remain accepted after end().
findings.trigger: Call write(Buffer.from("b")) after end(); even an empty write must throw.
findings.remedy: Check the ended flag at the start of write() and throw if set.

findings.issue: Decoding each chunk independently corrupts UTF-8 characters that span chunks.
findings.trigger: Writing Buffer.from([0xC3]) followed by Buffer.from([0xA9, 0x0A]) emits replacement characters instead of "é".
findings.remedy: Use a persistent UTF-8 decoder across writes and flush it during end().

findings.issue: Only LF is recognized; CRLF retains the CR in output, and standalone CR does not delimit lines.
findings.trigger: Writing "a\r\nb\rc" emits "a\r" and leaves "b\rc" pending. The required lines are "a", "b", and finally "c" at end.
findings.remedy: Recognize LF, CRLF, and standalone CR, retaining enough state to count a CR followed by LF across chunks only once.

findings.issue: end() unconditionally emits an empty line, including after a delimiter and on repeated calls.
findings.trigger: Writing "a\n" then calling end() emits an extra empty line. Calling end() on a fresh instance or calling it again also emits an unwanted empty line.
findings.remedy: Make end() idempotent and emit the final unterminated remainder only when nonempty.

findings.issue: Writes remain accepted after end().
findings.trigger: Calling end() followed by write(Buffer.from("x\n")) emits "x" instead of throwing.
findings.remedy: Track whether the instance has ended and reject every subsequent write, including empty writes.

findings.issue: Cache identity omits tenant and archived, and delimiter joining aliases distinct label sets, allowing requests to receive another request's data.
findings.trigger: Different tenants with the same labels share an entry; archived true and false share an entry; labels ['a,b'] and ['a', 'b'] also share an entry.
findings.remedy: Use a collision-safe key such as JSON.stringify([tenant, normalizedLabels, query.archived]), where normalizedLabels contains sorted unique labels.

findings.issue: Normalization mutates caller input, retains duplicates, and passes the caller's query to fetchReport instead of a fresh normalized query.
findings.trigger: Calling with labels ['b', 'a', 'a'] sorts the caller's array in place, forwards duplicate labels, and fails to share an entry with ['a', 'b']. Frozen label arrays can throw during sorting.
findings.remedy: Create a fresh query with labels: [...new Set(query.labels)].sort() and the unchanged archived flag; use it for both identity and loading.

findings.issue: Synchronous transport throws escape synchronously instead of becoming Promise rejections.
findings.trigger: fetchReport throws before returning; load executes before Promise.resolve is called, so createReports' returned function throws directly.
findings.remedy: Invoke load inside a Promise continuation, such as Promise.resolve().then(() => load(tenant, normalizedQuery)), and cache that Promise.

findings.issue: Rejected Promises remain cached permanently, preventing retries.
findings.trigger: fetchReport returns a rejected Promise; every subsequent equivalent request receives that same rejection without another fetch.
findings.remedy: Add rejection handling that deletes the entry only if it still contains the failing Promise, then rethrows the error. Preserve the shared Promise for pending and fulfilled requests.

findings.issue: The cache key omits tenant and archived, conflates delimiter-containing labels, and treats duplicate labels as significant.
findings.trigger: Different tenants or archived flags with identical labels share data; ['a,b'] collides with ['a','b']; ['a','a'] fails to share with ['a'].
findings.remedy: Key the Map with JSON.stringify([tenant, normalizedLabels, query.archived]), where normalizedLabels is sorted and unique. This also safely handles '__proto__'.

findings.issue: Sorting mutates caller input, and load receives the original query without deduplication or a fresh labels array.
findings.trigger: Any unsorted input is modified; frozen labels can throw; duplicate labels reach fetchReport unchanged.
findings.remedy: Create a fresh query with labels: [...new Set(query.labels)].sort() and archived: query.archived. Use it for identity and pass it to load with the original tenant.

findings.issue: Rejected promises remain cached permanently.
findings.trigger: After a transport rejection, subsequent equivalent requests return the same rejection instead of retrying.
findings.remedy: Attach rejection cleanup that deletes the key only if its current value is that entry's promise, then rethrows the error.

findings.issue: Synchronous transport throws escape synchronously; Promise.resolve(load(...)) in cache.mjs cannot catch argument-evaluation errors.
findings.trigger: fetchReport throws before returning a promise.
findings.remedy: Return Promise.resolve().then(() => fetchReport(tenant, query)) from requestReport so synchronous throws become promise rejections.

findings.issue: A cleanup exception replaces the source exception, violating the requirement to preserve source exceptions.
findings.trigger: If iterator.next() throws error A and iterator.return() throws error B, the finally block causes the consumer to receive B instead of A. A throwing return getter has the same effect.
findings.remedy: Track whether iteration threw and preserve that original exception while still attempting cleanup. Suppress cleanup failures only when preserving an existing iteration exception; otherwise propagate them.

findings.issue: The finally block can replace a source exception with an exception from iterator.return, violating the requirement to preserve source exceptions.
findings.trigger: iterator.next() (or a result's done/value getter) throws, then accessing or calling iterator.return also throws. The consumer receives the cleanup exception instead of the original source exception.
findings.remedy: Track whether iteration threw. Still attempt cleanup, but suppress cleanup errors when preserving an existing exception; otherwise propagate cleanup errors.

findings.issue: Older requests can overwrite results or status belonging to the latest submission.
findings.trigger: An earlier request resolves or rejects after a newer submission.
findings.remedy: Increment a submission counter on every submit and capture its value. After awaiting JSON, and in catch, update results/status only if the captured value is still current.

findings.issue: Blank submissions fetch instead of clearing results/status and invalidating pending requests.
findings.trigger: Submit empty or whitespace-only text, including while a request is pending.
findings.remedy: After incrementing the submission counter, trim the input. If empty, clear only results and status, then return without fetching.

findings.issue: Nonblank queries are neither trimmed nor URL-encoded.
findings.trigger: Submit surrounding whitespace or characters such as &, #, or +.
findings.remedy: Build the URL as '/search?q=' + encodeURIComponent(trimmedQuery).

findings.issue: Returned items are interpreted as HTML instead of rendered as text.
findings.trigger: An item contains markup such as 'hello' or an element with an event handler.
findings.remedy: Create an li for each item, assign its textContent, and replace only the results container's children.

findings.issue: Non-OK HTTP responses can incorrectly produce results and Ready status.
findings.trigger: A non-OK response contains valid JSON with an items array.
findings.remedy: Check response.ok before parsing JSON and throw on failure; let the guarded catch set Error for the latest submission.

findings.issue: Earlier requests can overwrite the latest query's results and status.
findings.trigger: Submit A, then B. If A resolves after B, A replaces B's results; if A rejects after B succeeds, it changes Ready to Error.
findings.remedy: Increment a submission generation on every submit. Capture it per request and guard result and status updates, including the catch path, against the current generation.

findings.issue: Blank submissions fetch and show Loading instead of clearing results/status and invalidating pending requests.
findings.trigger: Submit empty or whitespace-only text while an earlier request is pending. Another fetch starts, existing results remain, and the earlier request can still update the page.
findings.remedy: After invalidating earlier submissions, trim the input. If empty, clear only the results container and status, then return without fetching.

findings.issue: The submitted query is neither trimmed nor URL-encoded.
findings.trigger: Submitting '  a&b#c  ' introduces surrounding whitespace, an extra query parameter, and a URL fragment instead of sending the intended query value.
findings.remedy: Build '/search?q=' using encodeURIComponent on the trimmed nonblank query.

findings.issue: Returned items are interpreted as HTML instead of rendered as text.
findings.trigger: An item such as 'example' becomes markup; hostile markup can introduce executable event handlers.
findings.remedy: Create an li for each item, assign its textContent, and replace the results container's children with those nodes.

findings.issue: Non-OK HTTP responses can incorrectly produce Ready.
findings.trigger: A 404 or 500 response containing valid JSON with an items array is rendered as a successful response.
findings.remedy: Check response.ok before parsing JSON and throw on failure so the latest request's guarded error path displays Error.

findings.issue: A failed write displays the attempted value as saved and announces Saved, violating the success requirement.
findings.trigger: Select a different theme and submit when localStorage.setItem throws. #saved and status change before the write fails.
findings.remedy: Call setItem inside try/catch before updating #saved. On success, update #saved and show Saved. On failure, preserve #saved, show Could not save, and keep the controls usable for retry.

findings.issue: Unreadable storage aborts initialization without the required light fallback or a working submit handler.
findings.trigger: Accessing localStorage or calling getItem throws; execution stops before setting the selection and registering the submit listener.
findings.remedy: Initialize the restored value to light and guard storage access with try/catch. Continue initializing the display, selection, and submit handler after a read failure.

findings.issue: Invalid nonempty stored values are restored instead of falling back to light.
findings.trigger: The preference key contains a value such as blue. #saved displays blue and the select has no matching option.
findings.remedy: Accept only the exact stored values light and dark; use light for every other value.

findings.issue: Storage reads are unguarded, and invalid stored values are restored instead of defaulting to light.
findings.trigger: getItem or access to localStorage throws, preventing initialization and submit-handler registration; or storage contains a nonempty value other than light/dark.
findings.remedy: Initialize the restored value to light; inside try/catch, read preference and accept only light or dark. Then initialize #saved and the select and register the submit handler regardless of read failure.

findings.issue: The submit handler displays the new saved value and Saved before confirming the write, and never reports Could not save.
findings.trigger: localStorage access or setItem throws during submission.
findings.remedy: Read the selected value, attempt setItem("preference", value) inside try/catch, and update #saved and status to Saved only after success. On failure, leave #saved unchanged and set status to Could not save, keeping the controls usable for retry.

findings.issue: OutputRing.append decodes each chunk independently, so split UTF-8 characters become replacement characters. The per-stream decoders never receive bytes to buffer or flush.
findings.trigger: Append stdout bytes E2 82, append stderr text, then append stdout byte AC. The stdout character € is corrupted.
findings.remedy: Use this.decoders[stream].write(chunk) instead of chunk.toString("utf8"), retaining separate decoders and the existing raw-byte accounting, tail, and cursor logic.

findings.issue: Finalizing with a nonempty chunk counts and hashes its bytes but silently omits them from output.
findings.trigger: Call append("stdout", Buffer.from("last"), true); digests record four bytes while read returns no output.
findings.remedy: Pass chunk to this.decoders[stream].end(chunk) in the final branch so final bytes are decoded and pending bytes are flushed together.

findings.issue: Ordinary appends bypass the per-stream StringDecoders, so split multibyte UTF-8 characters remain corrupted.
findings.trigger: Append stdout bytes E2 82, append stderr text, then append stdout byte AC. The stdout chunks produce replacement characters instead of €; finalization cannot recover them because neither chunk entered the decoder.
findings.remedy: Decode ordinary chunks with this.decoders[stream].write(chunk), preserving the existing raw-byte accounting, tail storage, escaping, and cursor logic.

findings.issue: A chunk supplied with final=true is counted and hashed but silently omitted from output.
findings.trigger: append('stdout', Buffer.from('done'), true) records four raw bytes but emits no text because end() receives no chunk.
findings.remedy: Pass the optional final chunk to this.decoders[stream].end(chunk), allowing it to decode the last bytes and flush any incomplete sequence.

findings.issue: Admission counts only running tasks, violating the requirement that every task without confirmed cleanup occupies a slot.
findings.trigger: Call start five times before any supervisor reports started: all five tasks are admitted and spawned because starting tasks are excluded. Stopping and cleanup-unconfirmed tasks also fail to reserve capacity. Conversely, a task with confirmed cleanup and running status is incorrectly counted.
findings.remedy: Replace the status predicate with task.cleanup !== "confirmed". Preserve the closed check and synchronous guard before task-map insertion and spawning.

findings.issue: TaskRunner.start counts only running tasks, violating admission based on cleanup confirmation.
findings.trigger: Four tasks in starting, stopping, or cleanup-unconfirmed states still permit another spawn and task-map insertion. Conversely, a confirmed task with running status incorrectly consumes capacity.
findings.remedy: Replace the admission filter predicate `task.status === "running"` with `task.cleanup !== "confirmed"`, preserving the existing closed check and synchronous reservation.

findings.issue: VerificationRegistry.resolve captures current inputs but ignores their digest when determining freshness, so an obsolete receipt can still report passed. Two absent stored digests also compare equal.
findings.trigger: Record a successful receipt with matching before/after digests, then change a declared config or source file and resolve the receipt. It reports passed despite the changed current digest.
findings.remedy: Require all three digests to agree: const fresh = current.digest === receipt.before?.digest && current.digest === receipt.after?.digest; Preserve the existing outcome checks and stale/failed classification.

findings.issue: Freshness ignores the newly captured current digest, so a receipt can still report passed after a declared file changes. Missing before and after digests also compare equal.
findings.trigger: Record a successful outcome with matching before/after digests, modify a declared file, then resolve the receipt. captureInputs observes the change, but fresh only compares the stored snapshots and returns true.
findings.remedy: Require valid before and after digests and equality of current.digest, receipt.before.digest, and receipt.after.digest. Keep freshness failures stale and retain the existing four-part command-success predicate.

findings.issue: URL query secrets remain visible, so the requested fix is missing. Existing replacements handle other secret forms but never match URL query parameter names.
findings.trigger: redactCommand('curl "https://example.test/path?ToKeN=abc&view=full"') returns the command with abc exposed. The same applies to secret, password, api_key, api-key, and access_token query parameters, including mixed-case names.
findings.remedy: Add case-insensitive redaction for the specified URL query parameter values before truncation, preserving the URL path, parameter names, separators, non-secret parameters, and fragment. Retain the existing redaction behavior and UTF-8 truncation.

findings.issue: redactCommand leaves secret URL query parameter values visible. No redaction pass handles token, secret, password, api_key, api-key or access_token query parameters case-insensitively.
findings.trigger: For example, `curl 'https://example.com/path?ToKeN=abc&mode=fast#section'` exposes `abc` in the returned preview.
findings.remedy: Add a case-insensitive URL query parameter redaction pass before UTF-8 truncation that replaces only the specified parameters’ values with `[redacted]`, preserving parameter names, separators, other URL parts and existing redaction behavior.
